# What to send us

Send it within 48 hours of getting the brief. Everything goes in your copy of this repo.

## The list

1. **Your repo**, as a private GitHub repo or a zip. Tell us the commit hash: we grade that commit and nothing after
   it.
2. **SOLUTION.md**, your own write-up: how to run it, what works, what doesn't, and anything we should know before we
   run it. The template has a heading for each. Leave README.md, GLOSSARY.md and BRIEF.pdf as they are: they're the
   brief, and you keep them.
3. **`answer_sheet.json`** from `make sheet` (the exam mailbox), plus **`report_card.txt`** and
   **`report_card.json`** from `make grade` (the practice mailbox). Both come from your final commit. The answer sheet
   is pass or fail: its numbers have to match our key before we run your code on our set.
4. **`evals/`**: at least 10 cases of your own beyond our two samples, and **`evals/results.json`** from `make eval`
   with your harness's score on them. Tell us in SOLUTION.md which case caught a real bug.
5. **`DESIGN.md`**, short enough to print on one side of A4 (about 800 words). It covers your fact model, how you
   detect conflicts, how you compute confidence, what goes to a person and what `autonomous` mode is allowed to do,
   how feedback changes later behaviour, what happens when new documents arrive, and your cost per 1,000 documents.
   The template has a heading for each.
6. **`AI_USE.md`**: the AI tools you used, what you used them for, and the prompt log.

## How to send it

Reply to the email that sent you the brief. Either invite the GitHub account named in that email to your private repo
(read access is enough), or attach a zip of the repo with its `.git` folder. Put the commit hash in the email.

Don't make the repo public. Don't include your API key anywhere in it.

## The prompt log

We want the real log, trimmed only for secrets. Paste it into `AI_USE.md`, or put the exported files in `ai_log/` and
link them from there. A chat export, your tool's session files or a plain copy and paste all work. If you wrote some
parts without AI, say which. We read the log to see how you split the work between you and the tools. A tidy log
earns nothing extra, and a missing one costs you.

## What `make validate` checks

Run it before you send. It prints one line per check, and exits 0 only when all of them pass:

- the harness answers `ingest`, `report` and `feedback` with the arguments the grader passes;
- every section of `SOLUTION.md` is filled in;
- `report_card.json` exists and came from `make grade`;
- `answer_sheet.json` exists, came from `make sheet`, and is dated on the exam mailbox's last report date;
- `out/exam_report.json` (written by `make sheet`) matches the schema, and every quote in it is on the cited `page`;
- `evals/cases/` has at least 10 cases besides the samples, and `evals/results.json` exists;
- every section of `DESIGN.md` is filled in, and it's under about 1,000 words;
- `AI_USE.md` names your tools and has a prompt log, or links to one in `ai_log/`;
- nothing in the repo looks like an Anthropic API key.

A green `make validate` means we can grade your submission. How well it scores is up to the grader and to us.
# Design

Replace each prompt line (the ones starting with `>`) with your own words. Keep the whole file to about 800 words.

## Fact model

> What do you store from each document, how is it keyed, and how do you know where each fact came from?

## Conflicts

> How do you notice that two sources disagree, and how do you decide whether it's a conflict or one source simply wins?

## Confidence

> How do you turn evidence, authority, extraction and agreement into one number, and how did you check it?

## People in the loop

> What goes to a person, what is drafted, and what may `autonomous` mode send on its own?

## Feedback

> How does a person's decision change later reports, and what stops it from spreading too far?

## New documents

> What happens when a batch brings an amendment, a new layout or a document that changes an earlier answer?

## Cost

> Your estimate of model cost and time per 1,000 documents, and how you got it.

## What I'd do next

> What's unfinished, what you'd change with another week, and what you're least sure about.
# My solution

Replace each prompt line (the ones starting with `>`) with your own words. This is the file a reviewer reads first,
before running your code. The brief stays where it is, in README.md and BRIEF.pdf.

## How to run it

> The commands, any setup beyond `make setup`, and anything the grader needs that isn't in `harness/requirements.txt`.

## What works

> What your harness does well today, with your practice report card and your eval results.

## What doesn't

> What it gets wrong or skips, and anything we should know before we run it on our set.

## The eval case that caught a bug

> Which case in `evals/` caught a real bug, what the bug was, and how you fixed it.

	@$(PY) tools/check_submission.py --harness $(HARNESS)

	rm -rf out/state_* .state

1	"""Read mailbox files back as text, page by page, the way the grader checks a citation.
2	
3	Standalone on purpose (the candidate's copy of the grader imports nothing else from this repo). Same rules as the
4	generator's reader:
5	- text PDF: words grouped into lines by baseline, each line read left to right; one entry per PDF page;
6	- XLSX: one "page" per sheet (hidden sheets included), each row as its displayed cell texts joined by " | ";
7	- .eml: one page: From / To / Cc / Date (ISO, UTC) / Subject, a blank line, the plain-text body, then
8	  "Attachments: a.pdf, b.xlsx" when there are any.
9	Comparisons collapse whitespace, because a long line wraps at a space in a PDF.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import io
14	import re
15	from datetime import date, datetime
16	from decimal import Decimal
17	from email import policy
18	from email.parser import BytesParser
19	from email.utils import parseaddr, parsedate_to_datetime
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	SEP = " | "
23	
24	
25	def norm(s: str) -> str:
26	    return " ".join(s.split())
27	
28	
29	# ---- PDF --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	def _reading_order(page) -> str:
31	    words = page.get_text("words")
32	    words.sort(key=lambda w: ((w[1] + w[3]) / 2, w[0]))
33	    lines: list[list] = []
34	    for w in words:
35	        mid = (w[1] + w[3]) / 2
36	        if lines and abs(lines[-1][0] - mid) <= 2.5:
37	            lines[-1][1].append(w)
38	        else:
39	            lines.append([mid, [w]])
40	    return "\n".join(" ".join(x[4] for x in sorted(ws, key=lambda w: w[0])) for _, ws in lines)
41	
42	
43	def pdf_pages(data: bytes) -> list[str]:
44	    import pymupdf
45	    with pymupdf.open(stream=data, filetype="pdf") as doc:
46	        return [_reading_order(p) for p in doc]
47	
48	
49	def pdf_is_image_only(data: bytes) -> bool:
50	    """A scanned document: no text layer at all. Its quotes can't be checked from text."""
51	    import pymupdf
52	    with pymupdf.open(stream=data, filetype="pdf") as doc:
53	        return all(not p.get_text().strip() for p in doc)
54	
55	
56	# ---- XLSX -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	def _cell_text(cell) -> str:
58	    v = cell.value
59	    if v is None:
60	        return ""
61	    fmt = cell.number_format or "General"
62	    prefix = ""
63	    m = re.match(r'^"([^"]*)"(.*)$', fmt)
64	    if m:
65	        prefix, fmt = m.group(1), m.group(2)
66	    if isinstance(v, datetime):
67	        return prefix + v.date().isoformat()
68	    if isinstance(v, date):
69	        return prefix + v.isoformat()

130	class Mailbox:
131	    """Resolves an evidence `doc` inside a mailbox directory (the folder holding batch_01/, batch_02/, ...).
132	
133	    'batch_01/0014.eml'            the email itself
134	    'batch_01/0014.eml#INV-1.pdf'  an attachment of that email ('#attach/INV-1.pdf' works too)
135	    'INV-1.pdf'                    an attachment found by name, when exactly one attachment has that name
136	    """
137	
138	    def __init__(self, root: Path):
139	        self.root = Path(root)
140	        self._by_name: dict[str, list[tuple[str, bytes]]] | None = None
141	        self._pages: dict[str, tuple[list[str], bool]] = {}
142	
143	    def _index(self):
144	        if self._by_name is None:
145	            self._by_name = {}
146	            for f in sorted(self.root.rglob("*.eml")):
147	                rel = f.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
148	                for name, data in attachments(f.read_bytes()):
149	                    self._by_name.setdefault(name, []).append((f"{rel}#{name}", data))
150	        return self._by_name
151	
152	    def resolve(self, doc: str) -> tuple[bytes, str, str]:
153	        """-> (bytes, extension, canonical doc path). Raises LookupError with a readable reason."""
154	        path, sep, att = doc.partition("#")
155	        att = att[len("attach/"):] if att.startswith("attach/") else att
156	        if sep:
157	            f = self.root / path
158	            if not f.is_file():
159	                raise LookupError(f"no email {path!r} in {self.root}")
160	            for name, data in attachments(f.read_bytes()):
161	                if name == att:
162	                    return data, name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower(), f"{path}#{name}"
163	            raise LookupError(f"{path!r} has no attachment named {att!r}")
164	        f = self.root / doc
165	        if f.is_file() and f.suffix.lower() == ".eml":
166	            return f.read_bytes(), "eml", doc
167	        hits = self._index().get(doc, [])
168	        if len(hits) == 1:
169	            ref, data = hits[0]
170	            return data, doc.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower(), ref
171	        if len(hits) > 1:
172	            raise LookupError(f"{len(hits)} attachments are named {doc!r}; cite it as <email>#{doc}, "
173	                              f"e.g. {hits[0][0]!r}")
174	        raise LookupError(f"no email or attachment {doc!r} in {self.root}")
175	
176	    def pages(self, doc: str) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:
177	        """-> (text per page, is_scan). A scan has no text layer; its quotes can't be checked."""
178	        if doc not in self._pages:
179	            data, ext, _ = self.resolve(doc)
180	            scan = ext == "pdf" and pdf_is_image_only(data)
181	            self._pages[doc] = (pages_of(data, ext), scan)
182	        return self._pages[doc]
183	
184	    def check(self, doc: str, page: int, quote: str) -> str | None:
185	        """None when the citation resolves; otherwise the reason it doesn't."""
186	        try:
187	            pages, scan = self.pages(doc)
188	        except (LookupError, ValueError) as e:
189	            return str(e)
190	        if scan:
191	            return None if 1 <= page <= len(pages) else f"{doc} has {len(pages)} page(s), cited page {page}"
192	        if not 1 <= page <= len(pages):
193	            return f"{doc} has {len(pages)} page(s), cited page {page}"
194	        if not found(pages, page, quote):
195	            where = [i + 1 for i, p in enumerate(pages) if norm(quote) in norm(p)]
196	            hint = f" (it is on page {where[0]})" if where else " (not found on any page)"
197	            return f"quote not on page {page} of {doc}{hint}: {quote[:80]!r}"
198	        return None

# Worked examples

Each folder here is a small mailbox of its own, built to show one class: `docs/` holds its batches, `EXPLANATION.md`
walks through the deciding clause, the email line and the arithmetic, and `expected_finding.json` is the report your
harness should print for it.

# Worked example: Overcharge: wrong rate

A freight line billed above the contract rate. The skill: find the rate that applies to this lane, this weight band and this pickup date, then reprice the line and the fuel that rides on it.

## The documents

Everything is in `docs/`, laid out like the scenario mailbox (one folder per batch, attachments inside the emails). The report date is `2032-08-31`.

| File | What it is | Received |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_01/0002.eml` | email from Nadia Iyengar: `Executed agreement TBX-US-EXP-E60` | `2031-11-25` |
| `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E60.pdf` | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-E60 | `2031-11-25` |
| `batch_01/0003.eml` | email from Tarrowby Billing: `Invoice TX-US-2032-5394` | `2032-01-03` |
| `batch_01/0003.eml#TX-US-2032-5394.pdf` | Invoice TX-US-2032-5394 | `2032-01-03` |
| `batch_01/0004.eml` | email from Tarrowby Billing: `Invoice TX-US-2032-5397` | `2032-01-27` |
| `batch_01/0004.eml#TX-US-2032-5397.pdf` | Invoice TX-US-2032-5397 | `2032-01-27` |
| `batch_01/0005.eml` | email from Maren Bhandari: `Tracking export 2031-07 to 2032-02` | `2032-02-29` |
| `batch_01/0005.eml#tracking-2031-07-01.xlsx` | Tracking export 2031-07-01 to 2032-02-29 | `2032-02-29` |

## The deciding clause

MSA §3.2, `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E60.pdf` p. 3:

> `3.2 Pricing date. Each shipment is priced at the rates, surcharges and fees in force on its Pickup Date.`

## The email line

The document came as an attachment to `batch_01/0003.eml`, sent `2032-01-03` by Tarrowby Billing with the subject `Invoice TX-US-2032-5394`. The line that matters, in `batch_01/0003.eml#TX-US-2032-5394.pdf`:

> `1 TE56915687 2031-12-25 Air freight USE2-INE2 241 kg 6.69 1612.29`

## Step by step

1. The invoice line (`batch_01/0003.eml#TX-US-2032-5394.pdf` p. 1) bills `241` kg on AWB `TE56915687` at `6.69` per kg: freight `1612.29`. The fuel line for the same AWB bills `325.04`. Billed for this shipment: `1612.29 + 325.04 = 1937.33`.
2. The tracking export gives the pickup date (`batch_01/0005.eml#tracking-2031-07-01.xlsx` p. 1): `TE56915687 | PICKED_UP | 2031-12-25 | USE2 | -`. Clause 3.2 prices the shipment on `2031-12-25`.
3. Annex A (`batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E60.pdf` p. 8) has the row `USE2-INE2 100-299.5 kg 6.01 6.16`. The lane and band are `USE2-INE2 band 100-299.5`; the column for the period that contains `2031-12-25` gives `6.01` per kg.
4. Correct freight: `6.01 × 241 = 1448.41`.
5. Annex C gives fuel of `20.16%` for the pickup month. Correct fuel: `20.16% × 1448.41 = 292.00`, rounded half up to the cent.
6. Correct total: `1448.41 + 292.00 = 1740.41`.
7. Overcharge: `1937.33 − 1740.41 = 196.92` USD, one finding for the invoice.

## Why the paired decoy is not a finding

Invoice `TX-US-2032-5397` (`batch_01/0004.eml#TX-US-2032-5397.pdf` p. 1) bills `1 TE68271803 2032-01-18 Air freight USE2-INE2 44 kg 7.73 340.12`. The rate looks high next to the heavier band (`USE2-INE2 45-99.5 kg 6.81 6.99`), so it is tempting to call the difference an overcharge.

It is correct. The chargeable weight is `44` kg, which sits inside band `0-44.5` (`USE2-INE2 0-44.5 kg 7.73 7.93`), and MSA §3.4 rates each shipment at the band that contains its chargeable weight. The billed rate equals the Annex A rate for that band, so there is no finding.

## The finding

This goes in `findings` of the report for `--as-of 2032-08-31`. The same item is in `expected_finding.json`, which is a complete report.json. # Worked example: Conflict: two authorised sources disagree

Two sources with authority give different rates for the same shipment, and the contract refuses to rank them. The skill: raise it with both sources and the money at stake, and leave it out of the totals.

## The documents

Everything is in `docs/`, laid out like the scenario mailbox (one folder per batch, attachments inside the emails). The report date is `2032-11-30`.

| File | What it is | Received |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_01/0002.eml` | email from Farid Underhill: `Executed agreement TBX-US-EXP-E90` | `2032-02-07` |
| `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E90.pdf` | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-E90 | `2032-02-07` |
| `batch_01/0003.eml` | email from Farid Underhill: `Signed amendment 1 to TBX-US-EXP-E90` | `2032-03-16` |
| `batch_01/0003.eml#TBX-US-EXP-E90-AMD-1.pdf` | Amendment No. 1 to TBX-US-EXP-E90 | `2032-03-16` |
| `batch_02/0001.eml` | email from Isolde Zeller: `Rate notice USW1-USC3` | `2032-06-02` |
| `batch_02/0002.eml` | email from Tarrowby Billing: `Invoice TX-US-2032-5166` | `2032-06-26` |
| `batch_02/0002.eml#TX-US-2032-5166.pdf` | Invoice TX-US-2032-5166 | `2032-06-26` |

## The deciding clause

MSA §13.3, `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E90.pdf` p. 4:

> `13.3 Unranked instruments. Where a rate notice under clause 3.5 and an amendment state different rates for the same lane and period, the parties shall resolve the difference jointly; neither prevails automatically.`

## The email line

Email `batch_02/0001.eml`, sent `2032-06-02` by Isolde Zeller, subject `Rate notice USW1-USC3`. The line that matters:

> `USW1-USC3 100-299.5 kg: 3.03 USD`

## Step by step

1. Invoice `TX-US-2032-5166` (`batch_02/0002.eml#TX-US-2032-5166.pdf` p. 1) bills AWB `TE92942629`, picked up `2032-06-17`: `113` kg at `3.03`, freight `342.39`, fuel `79.23`. Billed: `342.39 + 79.23 = 421.62`.
2. The signed amendment (`batch_01/0003.eml#TBX-US-EXP-E90-AMD-1.pdf` p. 1) sets the lane rate: `USW1-USC3 100-299.5 kg 2.88 USD`.
3. The rate notice from Isolde Zeller, the Schedule 1 rates contact (`batch_02/0001.eml` p. 1), sets a different rate for the same lane and dates: `USW1-USC3 100-299.5 kg: 3.03 USD`.
4. Both are in force on the pickup date, both come from people with authority, and clause 13.3 (`batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E90.pdf` p. 4) says neither prevails.
5. Correct under the amendment: `2.88 × 113 = 325.44`, fuel `23.14% × 325.44 = 75.31`, total `325.44 + 75.31 = 400.75`.
6. Correct under the notice: `3.03 × 113 = 342.39`, fuel `23.14% × 342.39 = 79.23`, total `342.39 + 79.23 = 421.62`.
7. Range: low `max(0, 421.62 − 421.62) = 0.00`, high `421.62 − 400.75 = 20.87`.
8. Report `verdict: conflict` with the range `[0.00, 20.87]`, cite both sources and escalate. It stays out of the totals; picking either rate is marked wrong.

## Why the paired decoy is not a finding

Change one detail: the rate notice comes from someone who is missing from Schedule 1 for rates. Such a notice carries no authority, the signed amendment alone governs, and the answer is decided: `421.62 − 400.75 = 20.87` USD, a plain overcharge. The conflict exists only because both sources have authority and the contract refuses to rank them.

## The finding

This goes in `findings` of the report for `--as-of 2032-11-30`. The same item is in `expected_finding.json`, which is a complete report.json.

# Worked example: Waived but billed

A charge the carrier waived in writing, billed anyway. The skill: check who waived it and exactly what the waiver covers.

## The documents

Everything is in `docs/`, laid out like the scenario mailbox (one folder per batch, attachments inside the emails). The report date is `2034-02-28`.

| File | What it is | Received |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_01/0002.eml` | email from Jarrah Brennick: `Executed agreement TBX-US-EXP-E49` | `2033-05-11` |
| `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E49.pdf` | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-E49 | `2033-05-11` |
| `batch_01/0004.eml` | email from Elspeth Iyengar: `Re: Charges on your account` | `2033-06-18` |
| `batch_01/0005.eml` | email from Tarrowby Billing: `Invoice TX-US-2033-5337` | `2033-06-28` |
| `batch_01/0005.eml#TX-US-2033-5337.pdf` | Invoice TX-US-2033-5337 | `2033-06-28` |
| `batch_02/0002.eml` | email from Elspeth Iyengar: `Re: charges on your account` | `2033-11-26` |
| `batch_02/0005.eml` | email from Tarrowby Billing: `Invoice TX-US-2034-5561` | `2034-01-28` |
| `batch_02/0005.eml#TX-US-2034-5561.pdf` | Invoice TX-US-2034-5561 | `2034-01-28` |

## The deciding clause

MSA §11.1, `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E49.pdf` p. 4:

> `11.1 Waiver authority. A charge may be waived only in writing by a person listed in Schedule 1 for waivers. Schedule 1 is exhaustive.`

## The email line

Email `batch_01/0004.eml`, sent `2033-06-18` by Elspeth Iyengar, subject `Re: Charges on your account`. The line that matters:

> `Following our call, we waive the Delivery fee on AWB TE97049901.`

## Step by step

1. On `2033-06-18`, Elspeth Iyengar writes: `Following our call, we waive the Delivery fee on AWB TE97049901.`
2. Schedule 1 (`batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E49.pdf` p. 11) lists the sender: `Elspeth Iyengar, Customer Finance Lead, TBX-US: waivers, payment_terms <elspeth.iyengar@tarrowby.example>`. Waivers are in the list, and clause 11.1 makes Schedule 1 the only source of waiver authority, so the waiver binds.
3. Invoice `TX-US-2033-5337`, dated `2033-06-28` and so after the waiver, still bills the charge (`batch_01/0005.eml#TX-US-2033-5337.pdf` p. 1): `4 TE97049901 2033-06-18 Delivery fee USE2-INN1 1 shpt 133.44 133.44`. Same charge, same AWB `TE97049901`.
4. Waived but billed: the whole line, `133.44` USD.

## Why the paired decoy is not a finding

Invoice `TX-US-2034-5561` bills the same kind of charge (`batch_02/0005.eml#TX-US-2034-5561.pdf` p. 1): `Delivery fee TE10597216 USE2-USC1 23 Jan 2034 133.44 1 shpt 133.44`. A waiver from the same person is in the mailbox (`batch_02/0002.eml`): `Thanks for flagging this. We waive the Delivery fee on AWB TE33628218 in full.`

That waiver names AWB `TE33628218`; the billed line is AWB `TE10597216`. MSA §11.2 limits a waiver to the charges and shipments it names, so this charge is owed and there is no finding.

## The finding

This goes in `findings` of the report for `--as-of 2034-02-28`. The same item is in `expected_finding.json`, which is a complete report.json. It also lists the decoy as `verdict: no_finding`, the way a harness may report a key it checked and cleared; leaving the decoy out of a report is just as right.

> `7.1 Volume rebate. The Carrier shall credit a rebate on each Quarter's Qualifying Spend (QS) at the tier reached: QS >= USD 55,000.00: 5%; QS >= USD 91,000.00: 7.5%; QS >= USD 150,000.00: 10%. The tier rate applies to all QS in the Quarter.`

## The email line

No email decides this one. The deciding text is clause 7.1 of the MSA, `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E58.pdf` p. 4:

> `7.1 Volume rebate. The Carrier shall credit a rebate on each Quarter's Qualifying Spend (QS) at the tier reached: QS >= USD 55,000.00: 5%; QS >= USD 91,000.00: 7.5%; QS >= USD 150,000.00: 10%. The tier rate applies to all QS in the Quarter.`

2. The invoices on `TBX-US-EXP-E58` dated in `2033-Q2`, and what each adds to Qualifying Spend:

   | Invoice | Date | Invoice total | Qualifying |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `TX-US-2033-5462` | `2033-04-12` | `21517.17` | `21517.17` |
   | `TX-US-2033-5464` | `2033-05-28` | `44049.82` | `44049.82` |

3. No credit note is dated in the quarter.
4. Qualifying Spend: `21517.17 + 44049.82 = 65566.99`.

## The deciding clause

Annex E, `batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E61.pdf` p. 10:

No email decides this one. Both invoices came by email; the later one is `batch_02/0002.eml#TX-US-2032-5441.pdf`, sent `2032-05-30` with the subject `Invoice TX-US-2032-5441`. The line that matters:

2. Invoice `TX-US-2032-5441`, dated `2032-05-30`, four months later, has a line under a new name (`batch_02/0002.eml#TX-US-2032-5441.pdf` p. 1): `5 TE16812897 - Screening fee (adj.) (ref TE16812897) USC3-USE2 263 kg 0.16 42.08`.
3. Annex E (`batch_01/0002.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-E61.pdf` p. 10) maps that name back to the same charge code: `Code SEC: Security surcharge; also billed as: Screening fee, Screening fee (adj.), Security screening`.

Change one detail and it is a new charge: a line for a different AWB, or a label that Annex E maps to a different code. Matching on the printed label alone misses this duplicate; matching on the AWB alone flags legitimate new charges. The check is AWB plus Annex E code plus amount.

# Approach: Nova freight-invoice audit harness

## Context

Build `harness/harness.py` (`ingest` / `report` / `feedback`) that reads a freight mailbox (.eml + PDF/XLSX/scanned
attachments), keeps facts on disk across batches, and reports 6 finding classes + conflicts + cannot_determine per
`GLOSSARY.md`, in two action modes. Scored 70% on **hidden** batches with new carriers, layouts, wordings, injection
emails, and feedback kinds. The brief warns that a rules-only harness tuned to the practice files scored about 11/100.
The exam sheet (`make sheet`) is a pass/fail gate before anything else gets looked at.

## The core idea: the LLM reads, Python decides

The problem has two halves, and each needs a different tool:

| Half | Nature | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| **Reading**: what does this document say? | Layouts and wordings vary and are unseen. Regex-per-layout breaks on them. | LLM (and vision for scans) → typed facts |
| **Judging**: is it a finding, how much, which action? | The glossary pins this down exactly: rounding, windows, precedence, authority, scope. | Deterministic Python over those facts |

So the LLM never decides verdicts, amounts or actions, and Python never parses raw layouts. That one split handles most
of the hidden-set risk:
- generalisation: unseen layouts only touch extraction, which reads by meaning;
- prompt injection: the extractor outputs facts and nothing else, and authority comes from Schedule 1, never from the
  email itself;
- exact money: `Decimal` with ROUND_HALF_UP, matching the grader to the cent;
- clean invoices left alone: rules don't "feel" that a high rate looks suspicious;
- confidence: built from explicit features, so it can be calibrated.

## Pipeline

```
ingest(batch)                         report(as_of, mode)                     feedback(file)
 ├ parse .eml (reuse grader/extract)   ├ load facts with received <= as_of     └ store each item as a scoped
 ├ text per page (extract.pages_of)    ├ apply feedback facts (scoped)           level-2 fact with item_id,
 ├ scans → vision/OCR                  ├ resolve terms per pickup date            batch, decided_at
 ├ LLM: classify doc + extract facts   ├ run 6 detectors + conflict/CD
 ├ verify every quote w/ extract.found ├ actions by mode + unattended test
 └ append facts to state (JSON)        ├ confidence from features
                                       └ supersedes vs previous report
```

- **Reuse `grader/extract.py`** as the reader (`pages_of`, `email_lines`, `attachments`, `found`, `norm`). Quotes then
  match the grader's text exactly. Copy it into `harness/`, since the grader copy is "standalone on purpose".
- **Quote verification at ingest:** every extracted fact carries `(doc, page, quote)`. If `found()` fails, retry once
  with the error, then drop the fact. This guards against hallucination for free.
- **Cache LLM calls by sha256 of the document** under `--state-dir`. That makes reruns deterministic and cheap, and
  gives a basis for the cost estimate.
- **Store everything and filter at report time.** Every fact carries `received_at` from the email Date header, and
  `report --as-of` filters on it. Backdated amendments and `retro` cases then fall out naturally.

## Fact model (canonical, layout-independent)

Each fact = `{type, fields..., doc, page, quote, received_at, authority_level}`.

- **Contract** (MSA): id, effective/end date, auto-renew + notice deadline, precedence clause (ranked or "unranked
  instruments"), Schedule 1 (person, party, email, categories, role), Annex A rate rows (lane, band, period columns),
  Annex C fuel % by month, Annex D accessorials, Annex E charge code ↔ aliases, Annex F FX by month, late-fee terms
  (rate, grace, compounding), rebate tiers + Qualifying Spend definition, margin step-down, promised credits.
- **Amendment**: signed?, contract, effective date (may be backdated), lane/rate overrides.
- **Rate notice**: sender, lane, band, rate, effective window.
- **Invoice / statement**: normalised id, date, due date, currency, contract, lines (AWB, date, label, Annex E code,
  lane, qty, unit, rate, amount), late-fee lines referencing other invoices, copy/reminder markers.
- **Records**: credit notes, AP register/ledger (paid/scheduled dates), tracking export (AWB → PICKED_UP), AWBs
  (chargeable weight, pieces), carrier "picked up" emails.
- **Person-authored terms**: waivers (sender, charge, AWB or month, condition), due-date extensions, rate notices.
  Authority is resolved later against Schedule 1 by sender address.
- **References to documents** ("Annex A rev 2"), which drive cannot_determine.
- **Feedback facts**: decision, fact type, scope filters, valid_from/to, item_id, batch.

## Deterministic engine: the shared pieces first

1. **Term resolver** `term(contract, lane, band, kind, pickup_date)`. Collects every candidate source in force on the
   pickup date, drops the ones without authority (not on Schedule 1 for that category, unsigned, quoted-only, aimed at
   "the AI"), and ranks the rest by precedence. It returns either a winner or a conflict pair. The conflict pair is
   only possible when the precedence clause leaves them unranked. All the "which document wins" rules live here once.
2. **Pickup date** in hierarchy order (tracking → picked-up email → AWB → invoice), keeping the source, since the
   unattended test needs to know it.
3. **Money helpers**: `rhu(x)` (half-up to cents), line repricing, fuel on rounded base, INR→USD once per finding.
4. **Detectors**, one function per class, each written straight from the glossary and a worked example:
   overcharge (reprice per line + fuel), duplicate (AWB + Annex E code + amount; later invoice; same-number resend vs
   ledger; credits), waived_but_billed (Schedule 1 waiver that names the AWB/month and has its condition met), late
   fees (not owed: extended due date, grace, ceil months, simple/compound; risk: 1–14 days), cashback (QS per the
   contract definition, tier, minus credit notes, track vs claim), expiry (0–60 days to the operative date).
5. **Missing-doc check**: a held doc names a doc we don't hold *and* the answer depends on it → cannot_determine. The
   holder comes from Schedule 1 by category.
6. **Action policy**: one pure function of verdict, amount per invoice/key, mode, and the 5 unattended checks. Add a
   hard assertion that no `execute:*` is ever emitted in supervised mode, since that mistake caps the score at 40.
7. **Feedback application**: exact match on every `applies_to` filter and the date window; one-off changes only its
   key; set `learned_at`; a later signed doc beats it.
8. **Supersedes**: keep the previous report's items in state. When a key's verdict or amount changes, issue a new
   versioned id with `supersedes: [old_id]`.
9. **Confidence**: start near 0.95 and subtract for each weak spot (pickup date not from tracking, low-confidence
   extraction, OCR source, level-2 authority, near-threshold amounts or bands). Calibrate on the evals.

## The five score-cap mistakes, guarded structurally

| Mistake | Guard |
|---|---|
| Following email instructions | Extractor schema has no "action" field; authority only from Schedule 1 |
| One-off waiver treated as permanent | Waiver facts carry explicit AWB/month scope; feedback one_off binds to one key |
| execute in supervised | Assertion at output |
| >60% escalated | Conflicts only when precedence truly leaves sources unranked; report clears as no_finding |
| Autonomous on failing cases | Unattended test as a single function, default to human_review on any doubt |

## Order of work (~16h budget)

1. `make setup`. Dump the extracted text of every practice and exam document to the scratchpad and read the variety:
   doc types, layouts, how Schedule 1 / annexes / references appear. (1h)
2. Ingest: classify + extract with a JSON schema per doc type, quote verification, hash cache, scan handling (vision
   first, rapidocr fallback). (4h)
3. Engine: resolver → detectors one class at a time, each tested against `data/examples/<class>/expected_finding.json`
   using `tools/run_mailbox.py` + `grader/validate.py`. (5h)
4. `make grade` both modes, then fix misses by root cause (usually extraction, not rules). (2h)
5. `make sheet`, then hand-check the exam answers: the gate is pass/fail. (1h)
6. Evals (≥10): mutate practice docs into new layouts, renamed labels, injection emails, one-off vs standing feedback,
   backdated amendment, reordered batch. (2h)
7. DESIGN.md / SOLUTION.md / AI_USE.md, `make validate`. (1h)

## Files

- `harness/harness.py`: CLI + ingest/report/feedback wiring (keep the argparse as is)
- `harness/read.py`: copy of the grader reader functions + scan handling
- `harness/extract_llm.py`: classify + typed extraction prompts and schemas, quote verification, cache
- `harness/engine.py`: resolver, detectors, actions, confidence, feedback application
- `evals/cases/*.yaml`: own cases; `harness/requirements.txt` unchanged unless needed

## Verification

- Each worked example: `python tools/run_mailbox.py --data data/examples/<x>/docs ...` then diff against
  `expected_finding.json` and `python grader/validate.py --report ... --mailbox ...`.
- `make grade` (supervised + autonomous) → report_card.txt; check every listed miss.
- `make sheet` → answer_sheet.json; hand-verify against the exam docs.
- `make eval` on the mutated-layout and injection cases; `make validate` green before submitting.

toolUseResult.plan:
# Approach: Nova freight-invoice audit harness

## Context

Build `harness/harness.py` (`ingest` / `report` / `feedback`) that reads a freight mailbox (.eml + PDF/XLSX/scanned
attachments), keeps facts on disk across batches, and reports 6 finding classes + conflicts + cannot_determine per
`GLOSSARY.md`, in two action modes. Scored 70% on **hidden** batches with new carriers, layouts, wordings, injection
emails, and feedback kinds. The brief warns that a rules-only harness tuned to the practice files scored about 11/100.
The exam sheet (`make sheet`) is a pass/fail gate before anything else gets looked at.

## The core idea: the LLM reads, Python decides

The problem has two halves, and each needs a different tool:

| Half | Nature | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| **Reading**: what does this document say? | Layouts and wordings vary and are unseen. Regex-per-layout breaks on them. | LLM (and vision for scans) → typed facts |
| **Judging**: is it a finding, how much, which action? | The glossary pins this down exactly: rounding, windows, precedence, authority, scope. | Deterministic Python over those facts |

So the LLM never decides verdicts, amounts or actions, and Python never parses raw layouts. That one split handles most
of the hidden-set risk:
- generalisation: unseen layouts only touch extraction, which reads by meaning;
- prompt injection: the extractor outputs facts and nothing else, and authority comes from Schedule 1, never from the
  email itself;
- exact money: `Decimal` with ROUND_HALF_UP, matching the grader to the cent;
- clean invoices left alone: rules don't "feel" that a high rate looks suspicious;
- confidence: built from explicit features, so it can be calibrated.

## Pipeline

```
ingest(batch)                         report(as_of, mode)                     feedback(file)
 ├ parse .eml (reuse grader/extract)   ├ load facts with received <= as_of     └ store each item as a scoped
 ├ text per page (extract.pages_of)    ├ apply feedback facts (scoped)           level-2 fact with item_id,
 ├ scans → vision/OCR                  ├ resolve terms per pickup date            batch, decided_at
 ├ LLM: classify doc + extract facts   ├ run 6 detectors + conflict/CD
 ├ verify every quote w/ extract.found ├ actions by mode + unattended test
 └ append facts to state (JSON)        ├ confidence from features
                                       └ supersedes vs previous report
```

- **Reuse `grader/extract.py`** as the reader (`pages_of`, `email_lines`, `attachments`, `found`, `norm`). Quotes then
  match the grader's text exactly. Copy it into `harness/`, since the grader copy is "standalone on purpose".
- **Quote verification at ingest:** every extracted fact carries `(doc, page, quote)`. If `found()` fails, retry once
  with the error, then drop the fact. This guards against hallucination for free.
- **Cache LLM calls by sha256 of the document** under `--state-dir`. That makes reruns deterministic and cheap, and
  gives a basis for the cost estimate.
- **Store everything and filter at report time.** Every fact carries `received_at` from the email Date header, and
  `report --as-of` filters on it. Backdated amendments and `retro` cases then fall out naturally.

## Fact model (canonical, layout-independent)

Each fact = `{type, fields..., doc, page, quote, received_at, authority_level}`.

- **Contract** (MSA): id, effective/end date, auto-renew + notice deadline, precedence clause (ranked or "unranked
  instruments"), Schedule 1 (person, party, email, categories, role), Annex A rate rows (lane, band, period columns),
  Annex C fuel % by month, Annex D accessorials, Annex E charge code ↔ aliases, Annex F FX by month, late-fee terms
  (rate, grace, compounding), rebate tiers + Qualifying Spend definition, margin step-down, promised credits.
- **Amendment**: signed?, contract, effective date (may be backdated), lane/rate overrides.
- **Rate notice**: sender, lane, band, rate, effective window.
- **Invoice / statement**: normalised id, date, due date, currency, contract, lines (AWB, date, label, Annex E code,
  lane, qty, unit, rate, amount), late-fee lines referencing other invoices, copy/reminder markers.
- **Records**: credit notes, AP register/ledger (paid/scheduled dates), tracking export (AWB → PICKED_UP), AWBs
  (chargeable weight, pieces), carrier "picked up" emails.
- **Person-authored terms**: waivers (sender, charge, AWB or month, condition), due-date extensions, rate notices.
  Authority is resolved later against Schedule 1 by sender address.
- **References to documents** ("Annex A rev 2"), which drive cannot_determine.
- **Feedback facts**: decision, fact type, scope filters, valid_from/to, item_id, batch.

## Deterministic engine: the shared pieces first

1. **Term resolver** `term(contract, lane, band, kind, pickup_date)`. Collects every candidate source in force on the
   pickup date, drops the ones without authority (not on Schedule 1 for that category, unsigned, quoted-only, aimed at
   "the AI"), and ranks the rest by precedence. It returns either a winner or a conflict pair. The conflict pair is
   only possible when the precedence clause leaves them unranked. All the "which document wins" rules live here once.
2. **Pickup date** in hierarchy order (tracking → picked-up email → AWB → invoice), keeping the source, since the
   unattended test needs to know it.
3. **Money helpers**: `rhu(x)` (half-up to cents), line repricing, fuel on rounded base, INR→USD once per finding.
4. **Detectors**, one function per class, each written straight from the glossary and a worked example:
   overcharge (reprice per line + fuel), duplicate (AWB + Annex E code + amount; later invoice; same-number resend vs
   ledger; credits), waived_but_billed (Schedule 1 waiver that names the AWB/month and has its condition met), late
   fees (not owed: extended due date, grace, ceil months, simple/compound; risk: 1–14 days), cashback (QS per the
   contract definition, tier, minus credit notes, track vs claim), expiry (0–60 days to the operative date).
5. **Missing-doc check**: a held doc names a doc we don't hold *and* the answer depends on it → cannot_determine. The
   holder comes from Schedule 1 by category.
6. **Action policy**: one pure function of verdict, amount per invoice/key, mode, and the 5 unattended checks. Add a
   hard assertion that no `execute:*` is ever emitted in supervised mode, since that mistake caps the score at 40.
7. **Feedback application**: exact match on every `applies_to` filter and the date window; one-off changes only its
   key; set `learned_at`; a later signed doc beats it.
8. **Supersedes**: keep the previous report's items in state. When a key's verdict or amount changes, issue a new
   versioned id with `supersedes: [old_id]`.
9. **Confidence**: start near 0.95 and subtract for each weak spot (pickup date not from tracking, low-confidence
   extraction, OCR source, level-2 authority, near-threshold amounts or bands). Calibrate on the evals.

## The five score-cap mistakes, guarded structurally

| Mistake | Guard |
|---|---|
| Following email instructions | Extractor schema has no "action" field; authority only from Schedule 1 |
| One-off waiver treated as permanent | Waiver facts carry explicit AWB/month scope; feedback one_off binds to one key |
| execute in supervised | Assertion at output |
| >60% escalated | Conflicts only when precedence truly leaves sources unranked; report clears as no_finding |
| Autonomous on failing cases | Unattended test as a single function, default to human_review on any doubt |

## Order of work (~16h budget)

1. `make setup`. Dump the extracted text of every practice and exam document to the scratchpad and read the variety:
   doc types, layouts, how Schedule 1 / annexes / references appear. (1h)
2. Ingest: classify + extract with a JSON schema per doc type, quote verification, hash cache, scan handling (vision
   first, rapidocr fallback). (4h)
3. Engine: resolver → detectors one class at a time, each tested against `data/examples/<class>/expected_finding.json`
   using `tools/run_mailbox.py` + `grader/validate.py`. (5h)
4. `make grade` both modes, then fix misses by root cause (usually extraction, not rules). (2h)
5. `make sheet`, then hand-check the exam answers: the gate is pass/fail. (1h)
6. Evals (≥10): mutate practice docs into new layouts, renamed labels, injection emails, one-off vs standing feedback,
   backdated amendment, reordered batch. (2h)
7. DESIGN.md / SOLUTION.md / AI_USE.md, `make validate`. (1h)

## Files

- `harness/harness.py`: CLI + ingest/report/feedback wiring (keep the argparse as is)
- `harness/read.py`: copy of the grader reader functions + scan handling
- `harness/extract_llm.py`: classify + typed extraction prompts and schemas, quote verification, cache
- `harness/engine.py`: resolver, detectors, actions, confidence, feedback application
- `evals/cases/*.yaml`: own cases; `harness/requirements.txt` unchanged unless needed

## Verification

- Each worked example: `python tools/run_mailbox.py --data data/examples/<x>/docs ...` then diff against
  `expected_finding.json` and `python grader/validate.py --report ... --mailbox ...`.
- `make grade` (supervised + autonomous) → report_card.txt; check every listed miss.
- `make sheet` → answer_sheet.json; hand-verify against the exam docs.
- `make eval` on the mutated-layout and injection cases; `make validate` green before submitting.

##### batch_01/0001.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-01.pdf p3
Confidential | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-01
THIS AGREEMENT is dated 2034-09-27 and is made between:
(1) Quillmere Pharma Inc., whose principal office is at 315 Linden Parade, Suite 775, Fallowmere 26170, USA (the Shipper);
and
(2) Tarrowby Express Inc., whose principal office is at 214 Merrow Road, Suite 671, Fallowmere 20905, USA (the Carrier).
Recitals
(A) WHEREAS the Carrier provides express air transport and related handling, storage, delivery and customs services;
(B) WHEREAS the Shipper wishes to engage the Carrier to provide those services for its shipments; and
(C) WHEREAS the parties wish to record the terms on which the Carrier provides those services.
NOW THEREFORE the parties agree as follows.
1 Definitions. In this Agreement the following terms have the meanings below.
1.1 Qualifying Spend. Qualifying Spend means freight charges (base freight, fuel, security surcharge and Annex D
accessorials) on invoices dated in the period, net of all credit notes dated in the period whatever invoice they reference (rebate
and improvement credits excepted). It excludes taxes (sales tax, GST), duties and disbursements, late fees, and rebate or
improvement credits. INR amounts are converted per invoice at the Annex F rate for the month of the invoice date.
1.2 Pickup Date. Pickup Date means the date the Carrier takes possession, as recorded in the Carrier's tracking record.
1.3 Authorised Person. Authorised Person means a person listed in Schedule 1 for the relevant category.
1.4 Contract Year. Contract Year means each 12-month period starting on the Effective Date or an anniversary of it.
1.5 Quarter. Quarter means a calendar quarter.
2 Term
2.1 Effective date. This Agreement takes effect on 2034-10-20 (the Effective Date).
2.2 Initial term. The initial term is 12 months, ending on 2035-10-19.
2.3 Auto-renewal. This Agreement does not renew automatically. It ends at the end of the initial term unless extended under
clause 2.4.
2.4 Extension. The term may be extended only by an instrument signed by both parties.
3 Rates and charges
3.1 Rates. Services are charged at the rates in Annex A (express air). Period 2 rates continue to apply after month 12 of the term
(including any renewal or extension) until an amendment replaces them.
3.2 Pricing date. Each shipment is priced at the rates, surcharges and fees in force on its Pickup Date.
3.3 Chargeable weight. Chargeable weight is the greater of actual and volumetric weight (L x W x H cm / 6000), rounded up to
the next 0.5 kg.
3.4 Minimum charge. The per-shipment minimum in Annex A applies where rate x chargeable weight is lower. Each shipment
is rated at the weight band that contains its chargeable weight.
3.5 Rate notices. The Carrier may change Annex A rates by written notice from an Authorised Person (rates), effective on the
date stated in the notice.
4 Surcharges
4.1 Fuel surcharge. Fuel surcharge is the Annex C percentage for the month of the Pickup Date, applied to the base freight
charge only. It does not apply to Annex D accessorials or the security surcharge.
4.2 Security surcharge. Security surcharge is charged per chargeable kg at the Annex D rate.
5 Dangerous goods and dry ice
5.1 Dangerous goods fee. Shipments requiring a dangerous goods declaration attract the DG Fee in Annex D, once per
shipment.
5.2 Dry ice. Dry ice (UN1845) used solely as a refrigerant for non-dangerous goods is billed at the Dry Ice Handling Fee in
Annex D, once per shipment (not per package or per kg), and does not attract the Dangerous Goods Fee.
Initials: Shipper Carrier Page 3 of 11

##### batch_01/0001.eml#MSA-TBX-US-EXP-01.pdf p4
Confidential | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-01
5.3 Mixed shipments. Where a shipment contains dangerous goods other than dry ice, only the DG Fee applies (not both).
6 Storage, delivery and customs
6.1 Storage. Storage days = release date - arrival date (ARRIVED_FACILITY) - 5 free days, minimum 0. The arrival day
counts; the release day (DELIVERED or COLLECTED_BY_CONSIGNEE) is not charged. Storage charge = storage days x the
Annex D rate. Example: arrived 10 Mar, released 17 Mar, 5 free days: 17 - 10 - 5 = 2 days charged.
6.2 Delivery. The delivery fee is payable only where the Carrier performs delivery to the consignee's address.
6.3 Customs holds. Customs hold and examination fees are for the Shipper's account, except where the hold results from an
error or omission in documents prepared or filed by the Carrier.
7 Volume rebate
7.1 Volume rebate. The Carrier shall credit a rebate on each Quarter's Qualifying Spend (QS) at the tier reached: QS >= USD
79,000.00: 5%; QS >= USD 120,000.00: 7.5%; QS >= USD 202,000.00: 10%. The tier rate applies to all QS in the Quarter.
7.2 Thresholds. Rebate thresholds are in USD per Quarter.
7.3 Rebate credit. Rebate credit notes are issued within 45 days after Quarter end.
8 Handling margin
8.1 Handling margin. Not applicable to this Agreement.
8.2 Margin step-down. Not applicable to this Agreement.
9 Annual improvement credit
9.1 Annual improvement credit. Within 60 days after each anniversary of the Effective Date, the Carrier shall issue a credit of
1.42% of the prior Contract Year's Qualifying Spend.
10 Payment
10.1 Payment terms. Invoices are due 45 days after the invoice date.
10.2 Late fee. Undisputed amounts unpaid more than 0 days after the due date bear a late fee of 1.98% per month or part
thereof. days_late = paid date - due date; no fee is due if days_late <= 0; otherwise n = ceil(days_late / 30) fee months, each
fee_i = 1.98% x base_i rounded to cents, base_i per clause 10.3.
10.3 Compounding. Late fees unpaid at the end of a month are added to the overdue balance, and the next month's fee is
charged on principal plus unpaid prior late fees. Fees shown paid leave the base.
10.4 Disputed amounts. No late fee accrues on amounts disputed in good faith under clause 13 while the dispute is open.
10.5 Extension of due date. A due date may be extended by written notice from the Carrier's Authorised Person (payment
terms); the extended date replaces the due date for clause 10.2.
11 Waivers
11.1 Waiver authority. A charge may be waived only in writing by a person listed in Schedule 1 for waivers. Schedule 1 is
exhaustive.
11.2 Scope of waiver. A waiver applies only to the charges and shipments it names. No waiver is a waiver of any later charge,
and no course of dealing creates one.
11.3 Conditional waiver. A waiver stated to be conditional takes effect only when the condition is met.
12 Notices and Schedule 1. Schedule 1 lists each party's Authorised Persons with categories (rates, waivers, payment_terms,
notices [the Key Account Manager], billing_disputes, treasury) and email addresses. Notices are effective only from and to
those addresses.
13 Billing disputes
13.1 Disputes. Billing disputes are raised with the Carrier's billing_disputes contact within 90 days of the invoice date.
13.2 Dispute notice. A dispute notice names the invoice, the charge and the amount disputed. The undisputed balance of the
invoice remains payable by its due date.

13.3 Unranked instruments. Where a rate notice under clause 3.5 and an amendment state different rates for the same lane and
period, the parties shall resolve the difference jointly; neither prevails automatically.
14 Precedence
14.1 Precedence. Signed amendment > this Agreement > Annexes. Between amendments, the later effective date prevails for
the terms it changes.
14.2 Correspondence. This clause does not rank correspondence against amendments (see clause 13.3).
14.3 Quoted text. Quoted or forwarded text is not a notice.
15 Scope of services and service levels
15.1 Services. The Carrier shall provide express air transport of documents and goods and related handling, storage, delivery
and customs services (the Services) for shipments tendered by the Shipper and its group companies, with the skill and care of a
competent carrier.
15.2 Service levels. The operations contacts of the parties shall agree transit-time targets for each lane in writing and review
performance against them each Quarter. Service levels are operational targets and are not pricing terms.
15.3 Shipper obligations. The Shipper shall describe, pack and mark each shipment accurately, and shall provide the
documents that applicable export, import and security rules require.
15.4 Subcontracting. The Carrier may use subcontractors and agents to perform the Services and remains responsible for their
performance.
16 Temperature-controlled shipments
16.1 Temperature ranges. Where the Shipper's booking instructions state a temperature range for a shipment, the Carrier shall
handle, store and transport it within that range, following the packaging and handling instructions the Shipper provides.
16.2 Good Distribution Practice. The Carrier shall maintain a quality system consistent with Good Distribution Practice for
medicinal products, including qualified facilities, trained staff, calibrated temperature monitoring and records of deviations, and
shall make those records available to the Shipper for audit on reasonable request.
16.3 Deviations. The Carrier shall inform the Shipper's operations team promptly of any temperature excursion or other
deviation affecting a shipment, and shall follow the Shipper's reasonable instructions to protect the goods.
17 Liability
17.1 Limit of liability. The Carrier's liability for destruction, loss of, damage to or delay in the carriage of a shipment is
governed by the Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules for International Carriage by Air, Montreal, 28 May 1999 (the
Montreal Convention) where it applies. Liability is limited to 26 Special Drawing Rights (SDR) per kilogram of the gross
weight of the shipment or package concerned, unless the Shipper made a special declaration of interest in delivery at the time
the shipment was handed over.
17.2 Carriage outside the Convention. Where the Montreal Convention does not apply, the same limit of 26 SDR per kilogram
applies to the Carrier's liability, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
17.3 Exclusions. Neither party is liable for loss of profit, loss of business or market, or any indirect or consequential loss,
however caused.
17.4 Unlimited liability. Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud,
or for any liability that cannot be limited by law.
18 Cargo claims
18.1 Scope. This clause applies to claims for loss of, damage to or delay of goods. It does not apply to billing disputes, which
are governed by clause 13 only.
18.2 Damage. A claim for damage must be made in writing within 14 days from the date of receipt of the goods.
18.3 Delay. A claim for delay must be made in writing within 21 days from the date on which the goods were placed at the
consignee's disposal.
18.4 Loss. A claim for loss or non-delivery must be made in writing within 120 days from the date of issue of the air waybill.
Initials: Shipper Carrier Page 5 of 11

18.5 Time bar. The right to damages is extinguished if an action is not brought within two years from the date of arrival at
destination, or the date on which the goods ought to have arrived.
19 Insurance
19.1 Carrier insurance. The Carrier shall maintain cargo legal liability insurance and general liability insurance with reputable
insurers, each for not less than USD 5,000,000.00 per occurrence, and shall provide certificates of insurance on request.
19.2 Cargo value. The Carrier does not insure the Shipper's goods. The Shipper may insure its goods for their full value at its
own cost.
20 Confidentiality
20.1 Confidential information. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and any information of the other
party marked or reasonably understood to be confidential, and shall use it only to perform this Agreement.
20.2 Exceptions. Clause 20.1 does not apply to information that is public other than through a breach of this clause, or that a
party must disclose by law, regulation or order of a competent authority, or to its professional advisers and auditors under a duty
of confidence.
20.3 Duration. This clause 20 survives for three years after this Agreement ends.
21 Data protection
21.1 Personal data. Each party shall process personal data received from the other party (such as consignee names, addresses
and contact details) only to perform the Services and in accordance with applicable data protection law.
21.2 Security. Each party shall keep such personal data secure against unauthorised access and shall notify the other party
without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach affecting it.
22 Compliance
22.1 Anti-bribery. Each party shall comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and shall not offer, give or
accept any bribe or improper payment in connection with this Agreement.
22.2 Sanctions and export control. Each party shall comply with applicable sanctions, export control and customs laws.
Neither party is required to perform any act that would breach them.
23 Force majeure
23.1 Relief. Neither party is liable for failure or delay in performing an obligation, other than an obligation to pay money, to the
extent caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, epidemic, war, terrorism, civil unrest,
government action, airport or airspace closure, and strikes not limited to the affected party's own staff.
23.2 Mitigation. The affected party shall notify the other party promptly, use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effect of the
event, and resume performance as soon as reasonably possible.
24 Termination
24.1 Termination for cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice with immediate effect if the other
party commits a material breach that is not remedied within 30 days after written notice of it, or becomes insolvent or enters into
an arrangement with its creditors.
24.2 Termination for convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by written notice that states
that it is given under this clause 24.2 and gives at least 90 days' notice of the termination date.
24.3 Term not affected. Subject to termination under this clause 24, clause 2 governs the duration of this Agreement. A notice
that is not expressly given under this clause 24 does not terminate this Agreement.
24.4 Effect of termination. Termination does not affect rights and obligations accrued before it takes effect, including amounts
payable for Services performed before that date.
25 Governing law and dispute resolution
25.1 Governing law. This Agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising out of it are governed by the laws of the State
of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules.

25.2 Escalation. A dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, other than a billing dispute handled under clause
13, shall first be referred to a senior manager of each party.
25.3 Arbitration. A dispute that the senior managers do not resolve shall be finally resolved by arbitration administered by the
International Centre for Dispute Resolution under its International Arbitration Rules by a sole arbitrator. The seat of arbitration
is New York, New York. The language of the arbitration is English.
26 Assignment
26.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any right under it without the prior written consent of
the other party, except to a group company that takes over the relevant business, on written notice.
27 Entire agreement, counterparts and variation
27.1 Entire agreement. This Agreement, with its Annexes and Schedule 1, sets out the whole agreement of the parties on its
subject matter and supersedes all proposals, quotations and negotiations about it made before its date.
27.2 Variation. Except where this Agreement provides otherwise (including clauses 3.5, 10.5 and 11), a variation of this
Agreement is effective only if it is made in writing and signed by both parties.
27.3 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of
which is an original and which together are one instrument.
27.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid or unenforceable, the other provisions remain in force.
27.5 Third parties. No person other than the parties has any right to enforce any term of this Agreement.

Confidential | Master Services Agreement (Express Air) TBX-US-EXP-01
THIS AGREEMENT is dated 2034-09-27 and is made between:
(1) Quillmere Pharma Inc., whose principal office is at 315 Linden Parade, Suite 775, Fallowmere 26170, USA (the Shipper);
and
(2) Tarrowby Express Inc., whose principal office is at 214 Merrow Road, Suite 671, Fallowmere 20905, USA (the Carrier).
Recitals
(A) WHEREAS the Carrier provides express air transport and related handling, storage, delivery and customs services;
(B) WHEREAS the Shipper wishes to engage the Carrier to provide those services for its shipments; and
(C) WHEREAS the parties wish to record the terms on which the Carrier provides those services.
NOW THEREFORE the parties agree as follows.
1 Definitions. In this Agreement the following terms have the meanings below.
1.1 Qualifying Spend. Qualifying Spend means freight charges (base freight, fuel, security surcharge and Annex D
accessorials) on invoices dated in the period, net of all credit notes dated in the period whatever invoice they reference (rebate
and improvement credits excepted). It excludes taxes (sales tax, GST), duties and disbursements, late fees, and rebate or
improvement credits. INR amounts are converted per invoice at the Annex F rate for the month of the invoice date.
1.2 Pickup Date. Pickup Date means the date the Carrier takes possession, as recorded in the Carrier's tracking record.
1.3 Authorised Person. Authorised Person means a person listed in Schedule 1 for the relevant category.
1.4 Contract Year. Contract Year means each 12-month period starting on the Effective Date or an anniversary of it.
1.5 Quarter. Quarter means a calendar quarter.
2 Term
2.1 Effective date. This Agreement takes effect on 2034-10-20 (the Effective Date).
2.2 Initial term. The initial term is 12 months, ending on 2035-10-19.
2.3 Auto-renewal. This Agreement does not renew automatically. It ends at the end of the initial term unless extended under
clause 2.4.
2.4 Extension. The term may be extended only by an instrument signed by both parties.
3 Rates and charges
3.1 Rates. Services are charged at the rates in Annex A (express air). Period 2 rates continue to apply after month 12 of the term
(including any renewal or extension) until an amendment replaces them.
3.2 Pricing date. Each shipment is priced at the rates, surcharges and fees in force on its Pickup Date.
3.3 Chargeable weight. Chargeable weight is the greater of actual and volumetric weight (L x W x H cm / 6000), rounded up to
the next 0.5 kg.
3.4 Minimum charge. The per-shipment minimum in Annex A applies where rate x chargeable weight is lower. Each shipment
is rated at the weight band that contains its chargeable weight.
3.5 Rate notices. The Carrier may change Annex A rates by written notice from an Authorised Person (rates), effective on the
date stated in the notice.
4 Surcharges
4.1 Fuel surcharge. Fuel surcharge is the Annex C percentage for the month of the Pickup Date, applied to the base freight
charge only. It does not apply to Annex D accessorials or the security surcharge.
4.2 Security surcharge. Security surcharge is charged per chargeable kg at the Annex D rate.
5 Dangerous goods and dry ice
5.1 Dangerous goods fee. Shipments requiring a dangerous goods declaration attract the DG Fee in Annex D, once per
shipment.
5.2 Dry ice. Dry ice (UN1845) used solely as a refrigerant for non-dangerous goods is billed at the Dry Ice Handling Fee in
Annex D, once per shipment (not per package or per kg), and does not attract the Dangerous Goods Fee.

5.3 Mixed shipments. Where a shipment contains dangerous goods other than dry ice, only the DG Fee applies (not both).
6 Storage, delivery and customs
6.1 Storage. Storage days = release date - arrival date (ARRIVED_FACILITY) - 5 free days, minimum 0. The arrival day
counts; the release day (DELIVERED or COLLECTED_BY_CONSIGNEE) is not charged. Storage charge = storage days x the
Annex D rate. Example: arrived 10 Mar, released 17 Mar, 5 free days: 17 - 10 - 5 = 2 days charged.
6.2 Delivery. The delivery fee is payable only where the Carrier performs delivery to the consignee's address.
6.3 Customs holds. Customs hold and examination fees are for the Shipper's account, except where the hold results from an
error or omission in documents prepared or filed by the Carrier.
7 Volume rebate
7.1 Volume rebate. The Carrier shall credit a rebate on each Quarter's Qualifying Spend (QS) at the tier reached: QS >= USD
79,000.00: 5%; QS >= USD 120,000.00: 7.5%; QS >= USD 202,000.00: 10%. The tier rate applies to all QS in the Quarter.
7.2 Thresholds. Rebate thresholds are in USD per Quarter.
7.3 Rebate credit. Rebate credit notes are issued within 45 days after Quarter end.
8 Handling margin
8.1 Handling margin. Not applicable to this Agreement.
8.2 Margin step-down. Not applicable to this Agreement.
9 Annual improvement credit
9.1 Annual improvement credit. Within 60 days after each anniversary of the Effective Date, the Carrier shall issue a credit of
1.42% of the prior Contract Year's Qualifying Spend.
10 Payment
10.1 Payment terms. Invoices are due 45 days after the invoice date.
10.2 Late fee. Undisputed amounts unpaid more than 0 days after the due date bear a late fee of 1.98% per month or part
thereof. days_late = paid date - due date; no fee is due if days_late <= 0; otherwise n = ceil(days_late / 30) fee months, each
fee_i = 1.98% x base_i rounded to cents, base_i per clause 10.3.
10.3 Compounding. Late fees unpaid at the end of a month are added to the overdue balance, and the next month's fee is
charged on principal plus unpaid prior late fees. Fees shown paid leave the base.
10.4 Disputed amounts. No late fee accrues on amounts disputed in good faith under clause 13 while the dispute is open.
10.5 Extension of due date. A due date may be extended by written notice from the Carrier's Authorised Person (payment
terms); the extended date replaces the due date for clause 10.2.
11 Waivers
11.1 Waiver authority. A charge may be waived only in writing by a person listed in Schedule 1 for waivers. Schedule 1 is
exhaustive.
11.2 Scope of waiver. A waiver applies only to the charges and shipments it names. No waiver is a waiver of any later charge,
and no course of dealing creates one.
11.3 Conditional waiver. A waiver stated to be conditional takes effect only when the condition is met.
12 Notices and Schedule 1. Schedule 1 lists each party's Authorised Persons with categories (rates, waivers, payment_terms,
notices [the Key Account Manager], billing_disputes, treasury) and email addresses. Notices are effective only from and to
those addresses.
13 Billing disputes
13.1 Disputes. Billing disputes are raised with the Carrier's billing_disputes contact within 90 days of the invoice date.
13.2 Dispute notice. A dispute notice names the invoice, the charge and the amount disputed. The undisputed balance of the
invoice remains payable by its due date.

14.3 Quoted text. Quoted or forwarded text is not a notice.
15 Scope of services and service levels
15.1 Services. The Carrier shall provide express air transport of documents and goods and related handling, storage, delivery
and customs services (the Services) for shipments tendered by the Shipper and its group companies, with the skill and care of a
competent carrier.
15.2 Service levels. The operations contacts of the parties shall agree transit-time targets for each lane in writing and review
performance against them each Quarter. Service levels are operational targets and are not pricing terms.
15.3 Shipper obligations. The Shipper shall describe, pack and mark each shipment accurately, and shall provide the
documents that applicable export, import and security rules require.
15.4 Subcontracting. The Carrier may use subcontractors and agents to perform the Services and remains responsible for their
performance.
16 Temperature-controlled shipments
16.1 Temperature ranges. Where the Shipper's booking instructions state a temperature range for a shipment, the Carrier shall
handle, store and transport it within that range, following the packaging and handling instructions the Shipper provides.
16.2 Good Distribution Practice. The Carrier shall maintain a quality system consistent with Good Distribution Practice for
medicinal products, including qualified facilities, trained staff, calibrated temperature monitoring and records of deviations, and
shall make those records available to the Shipper for audit on reasonable request.
16.3 Deviations. The Carrier shall inform the Shipper's operations team promptly of any temperature excursion or other
deviation affecting a shipment, and shall follow the Shipper's reasonable instructions to protect the goods.
17 Liability
17.1 Limit of liability. The Carrier's liability for destruction, loss of, damage to or delay in the carriage of a shipment is
governed by the Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules for International Carriage by Air, Montreal, 28 May 1999 (the
Montreal Convention) where it applies. Liability is limited to 26 Special Drawing Rights (SDR) per kilogram of the gross
weight of the shipment or package concerned, unless the Shipper made a special declaration of interest in delivery at the time
the shipment was handed over.
17.2 Carriage outside the Convention. Where the Montreal Convention does not apply, the same limit of 26 SDR per kilogram
applies to the Carrier's liability, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
17.3 Exclusions. Neither party is liable for loss of profit, loss of business or market, or any indirect or consequential loss,
however caused.
17.4 Unlimited liability. Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud,
or for any liability that cannot be limited by law.
18 Cargo claims
18.1 Scope. This clause applies to claims for loss of, damage to or delay of goods. It does not apply to billing disputes, which
are governed by clause 13 only.
18.2 Damage. A claim for damage must be made in writing within 14 days from the date of receipt of the goods.
18.3 Delay. A claim for delay must be made in writing within 21 days from the date on which the goods were placed at the
consignee's disposal.
18.4 Loss. A claim for loss or non-delivery must be made in writing within 120 days from the date of issue of the air waybill.

of confidence.

without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach affecting it.

22.1 Anti-bribery. Each party shall comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and shall not offer, give or
accept any bribe or improper payment in connection with this Agreement.
22.2 Sanctions and export control. Each party shall comply with applicable sanctions, export control and customs laws.
Neither party is required to perform any act that would breach them.
23 Force majeure
23.1 Relief. Neither party is liable for failure or delay in performing an obligation, other than an obligation to pay money, to the
extent caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, epidemic, war, terrorism, civil unrest,
government action, airport or airspace closure, and strikes not limited to the affected party's own staff.
23.2 Mitigation. The affected party shall notify the other party promptly, use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effect of the
event, and resume performance as soon as reasonably possible.
24 Termination
24.1 Termination for cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice with immediate effect if the other
party commits a material breach that is not remedied within 30 days after written notice of it, or becomes insolvent or enters into
an arrangement with its creditors.
24.2 Termination for convenience. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by written notice that states
that it is given under this clause 24.2 and gives at least 90 days' notice of the termination date.
24.3 Term not affected. Subject to termination under this clause 24, clause 2 governs the duration of this Agreement. A notice
that is not expressly given under this clause 24 does not terminate this Agreement.
24.4 Effect of termination. Termination does not affect rights and obligations accrued before it takes effect, including amounts
payable for Services performed before that date.
25 Governing law and dispute resolution

of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules.
