tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_credit_usage
tools.description:
Get the authenticated Firecrawl team's current credit balance or historical credit consumption. Use the current view to answer how many credits remain or to check billing-period boundaries. Use the historical view for monthly usage reporting and trend analysis.

The current view returns `remainingCredits`, `planCredits`, `billingPeriodStart`, and `billingPeriodEnd`. Extra purchased or granted credits can make `remainingCredits` greater than `planCredits`. Billing-period dates may be null when the upstream billing provider has no period metadata.

The historical view returns periods sorted by start date with `startDate`, `endDate`, and `creditsUsed`. Set `byApiKey` to include separate periods per API key, identified by the optional `apiKey` field. The newest period's `endDate` can be null.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_feedback
tools.description:
Submit concise quality feedback for a completed search, scrape, parse, or map job. Provide the endpoint, job ID, rating, and relevant issue codes or small contextual fields; omit large page contents and raw outputs.

For an Alexandria session, set endpoint to `alexandria`, omit jobId, and provide requestedWebsite (url and requestedFunctionality), objective, rationale, and rating. objective is the underlying goal behind the session: what you or your user were ultimately trying to accomplish (for example, "shortlist federal IT contracts to bid on this quarter"), not only what was needed from this website. Optional providerFeedback and capabilityFeedback describe gaps or errors. Capability issues: new_capability_request (requires requestedFunctionality), missing_capability, insufficient_functionality, incorrect_result, execution_error, other. Alexandria feedback must arrive within 20 minutes of the team's latest Alexandria search, discovery, or execution; later feedback is rejected. Eligible feedback can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to daily caps per website and per team.

Returns submission status, feedback ID, and accounting fields.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
tools.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_gov_search
tools.description:
Search US federal, state, and local statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications for legal or regulatory questions that need primary text. Clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date before identifying the governing rule.

Returns ranked results with a position, title, URL, and matched snippet. Results may include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions. Verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law. Read a known URL or additional page context with firecrawl_scrape. Use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage; no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_interact
tools.description:
Open or reuse a live browser session to navigate a page, click controls, fill fields, or run browser code. Provide either `url` or `scrapeId`, and either a natural-language `prompt` or executable `code`; code can run as Bash, Python, or Node with a bounded timeout.

This acts on the live site, so actions such as form submission can create persistent external side effects. Returns execution output, stdout/stderr, exit status, and session viewing URLs.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Enumerate URLs indexed under one website through Firecrawl without fetching each page's content. Use this when the request asks for a site's URL inventory, when several relevant pages must be located, or when the desired page URL is unknown. An optional `search` term narrows the URL list, while sitemap, subdomain, query-parameter, and result-limit options control coverage.

Returns matching URLs rather than page bodies. Retrieve one page with `firecrawl_scrape`; collect content across multiple pages with `firecrawl_crawl`. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional map feedback.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_monitor_check
tools.description:
Retrieve one monitor check and its page-level results, optionally filtered by page status. Pages report `same`, `new`, `changed`, `removed`, or `error`; configured goal judging can add a meaningful-change decision.

Markdown tracking returns a unified text diff, JSON tracking returns field paths with previous/current values and a current snapshot, and mixed tracking returns both. Returns one page of results plus a `next` URL when more pages exist.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_monitor_create
tools.description:
Create a recurring scrape, crawl, or search monitor that compares each check with its retained predecessor. The simple form accepts `page`/`pages` or `queries` plus a plain-language `goal`; the advanced `body` form controls targets, schedule, change-tracking formats, judging, retention, webhook, and notifications.

In the simple form, a `goal` is required. If `queries` contains one or more non-empty values and is supplied with `page`/`pages`, `queries` create the search target and page targets are ignored. A monitor schedules future network checks and can send configured email or webhook notifications. Returns the created monitor.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_parse
tools.description:
Parse one supported document into markdown, HTML, links, summary, targeted answers, or JSON matching a schema. Supported inputs include common HTML, PDF, Word, RTF, OpenDocument, and spreadsheet files; PDF parsing can be bounded with `pdfOptions.maxPages`.

Local MCP reads `filePath` from the server filesystem. Hosted MCP uses two calls: first provide `filePath` to receive upload instructions, upload locally, then call again with the returned `uploadRef`; do not send both fields together. Remote web URLs belong in `firecrawl_scrape`.

Set `redactPII` to request redaction of personally identifiable information in the returned content. `zeroDataRetention` requires an eligible authenticated account; omit it for anonymous keyless use. Returns upload instructions for hosted phase one or parsed document content for the final call. Authenticated final responses can include a `data.metadata.scrapeId` for optional parse feedback.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session with Alexandria access, `firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call. Keyless sessions have no provider matches.

Alexandria mode, on an authenticated session with Alexandria access: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Query operators, domain filters, `categories`, `toolDetail` and `scrapeOptions` are described on their parameters. Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

schema.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_search
schema.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Query operators, domain filters, `categories`, `toolDetail` and `scrapeOptions` are described on their parameters. Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

objective.description: Optional broader goal for this search, if known. Avoid sensitive information.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

scrapeOptions.description: Attach page content for web results in the same call. These fetches ignore maxAge, so use firecrawl_scrape when you need a live fetch. scrapeOptions fetches web pages, never Alexandria provider tools.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

tools.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
tools.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable source, `partial` a valuable source or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableSources` and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

schema.name: mcp__firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
schema.description:

A `good` rating requires a valuable source, `partial` a valuable source or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableSources` and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

content.text:
No, not everything. Most of the list is handled, a few items are only partly handled, and one is a real gap I explained away too easily.

**Handled and tested**

| Pitfall | What I did |
|---|---|
| 1. Feedback scope | A standing fact must match every `applies_to` filter inside its dates. One-off approvals bind one key and the named months, and `close`/`reject` drop that key only. Eight eval cases cover this, including "March approved, April not" and authority confirmed for the wrong category. |
| 2. Injection | The extractor has no action field. Text aimed at automated readers goes to a separate field that changes nothing, and one eval case covers it. |
| 5. Supervised `execute` | `action()` can only return `execute:*` when the mode is autonomous, and the card shows the gate clear. I planned a hard assertion but never wrote one. |
| 7. Decoys | All 16 practice controls and my own near-misses are left alone. |
| 8. Scan | The scan is read by a vision model, and the transcription is arithmetically consistent. |
| 10. INR | Converted once per finding at the invoice month's Annex F rate. A missing month gives `cannot_determine` with the treasury holder (tested). |
| 3. Over-escalation | 4% on practice, against the 60% cap. |

**Partly handled**
- **4. Unattended-action test:** the pickup-source check applies to overcharges. For the other classes I mark `safe=True` unconditionally. That matches all 24 practice actions, but it isn't a full implementation of the five checks.
- **9. Holder:** the holder comes from Schedule 1, not from the email body. For a missing original email, I return the first person listed for that category, not the sender's own entry. That is wrong when a category has two contacts.
- **11. Practice exclusion:** my design handles it, since reports are rebuilt from facts. But I've only tested two batches, not the "three more months" growth the hidden set uses.

**Not done: 6. Margin step-down**
- The glossary defines it, and my extraction schema already captures its fields: percent, step-down percent and threshold.
- The engine skips `MARGIN` lines, so it doesn't invent per-invoice overcharges, which is the trap. But it also never reports the `margin_step_down` cashback.
- I wrote in SOLUTION.md that no contract I've seen has the clause. That's true of the 14 I checked, but the hidden set is built around the glossary, so I'd expect it to appear. I was wrong to treat it as optional.
- The formula is only partly specified: it is the sum of billed margin minus stepped-down margin on invoices after the threshold-crossing one, per quarter. I'd implement that reading and say plainly that I can't verify it against real data.

**One more caveat:** all of this was written by reading the glossary and grader. None of it has run against live extraction.

Should I implement margin step-down and fix the holder choice, both free? I'd also add the missing execute assertion, and I won't make any paid calls.

content.text:
The cached runs (`make grade`, `make sheet`, `make eval`) won't tell you anything new, because they replay the same cached extractions. Only a live API run adds information, and what it checks is narrow.

**What a live run would reveal**
- **Schema acceptance:** whether the API accepts the contract schema, which is large and nested, and whether the prompt-JSON fallback in `llm.py` ever triggers.
- **Extraction quality:** whether direct API extraction matches what the Claude Code subagents produced. The subagents read files with a tool and the API doesn't, so line references and values could differ.
- **Practical limits:** timeouts, token caps on long contracts, and rate limits at 12 parallel workers.

Whether the subagent and API extractions differ is the key unknown, because the grader only ever uses the API path.

**Free improvements first, so the paid run isn't wasted**
1. Implement margin step-down and say plainly that I can't verify it against real data.
2. Fix the missing-document holder so it's the sender's own Schedule 1 entry, not the first person in the category.
3. Add the hard assertion that no `execute:*` is ever emitted in supervised mode.
4. Make the autonomous safety check per class instead of `safe=True` for non-overcharge findings.
5. Test a longer batch sequence from the existing mailboxes, since the hidden set adds three more months.

**The live run itself, kept small**
- It would be one invoice, one contract, and the scanned invoice (about 3 calls). I'd diff the results field by field against the cached versions, so a mismatch shows up for free.
- A pass proves the path works. A fail is worth far more, because it would have broken everything in the grader.

**Not worth running:** a full-mailbox live run. It costs the most and adds little beyond the three-document check, unless that check shows differences.

I'll do the free items now. Do you have a working key for the three-call live check?

{"success":true,"data":{"web":[{"url":"https://docs.coupa.com/en/developer-documentation/coupa-core-flat-files-csv/flat-file-csv-export/invoices-export","title":"Invoices Export - Coupa Documentation","description":"The date of the invoice was marked as paid in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM. datetime, No/No. payment-notes, Text field for comments on ...","position":1},{"url":"https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/taxation/vat/vat-businesses/invoicing_en","title":"VAT Invoicing - Taxation and Customs Union - European Union","description":"# VAT Invoicing
- Electronic invoices are equivalent to paper invoices.
- Businesses are free to issue electronic invoices subject to acceptance by the recipient. However, for business-to-government (B2G) transactions, public administrations must accept structured electronic invoices.
- Businesses can outsource invoicing operations to a third party or to the customer (i.e. self-billing), in some circumstances.
- Businesses are generally free to store invoices where and how they like (paper/electronic, in a different EU Member State to where they are based, etc.).

For a detailed explanation of EU-wide invoicing, consult the [explanatory notes on VAT invoicing](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/document/download/12dc566c-9f43-49d9-a306-b706879104ba_en?filename=explanatory_notes_en.pdf).

For specific provisions approved by each EU Member State, visit the [Tax Information Communication database](https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/tic/public/index.html).

## When is an invoice compulsory?
There may also be specific national rules on transactions requiring an invoice.

**For B2C transactions**, a business must issue an invoice when it supplies certain goods to a non-taxable person (generally a private individual) in these cases:

**Specific national rules** apply in some EU Member States:

## What information must a VAT invoice contain?
| Full invoice | Simplified invoice |
|-|-|
| Date of issue | Date of issue |
| Unique sequential number identifying the invoice | - |
| Supplier’s full name & address | - |
| Customer’s full name & address | - |
| Customer’s VAT identification number (if the customer is liable for tax on the transaction) | Supplier’s VAT identification number |
| Date of transaction or payment (if different from invoice date) | - |
| VAT rate applied & amount payable | VAT amount payable (or the information needed to calculate it) |
| Breakdown of VAT amount payable by VAT rate or exemption | - |
| - | Specific, unambiguous reference to the initial invoice and the details that are being amended (on a credit note, debit note or other document treated as an invoice) |
| **Extra information required in some cases** |  |
| For exempt transactions: a reference to the appropriate (EU or national) legislation exempting it, or any other reference indicating it is exempt (at the choice of the supplier) |  |
| If the customer is liable for tax (i.e. under the reverse-charge procedure): the words ‘reverse charge’ |  |
| For intra-EU supply of a new means of transport: the details specified in Article 2(2)(b) of the [VAT Directive](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32006L0112) |  |
| If a margin scheme applies: a reference to the scheme involved (e.g. ‘margin scheme — travel agents’) |  |
| Self-billing (customer issues invoice instead of supplier): the words ‘self-billing’ |  |
| Supplier is operating a cash accounting system: the words ‘cash accounting’) |  |

Once all the information above is included on an invoice (depending on the case and EU Member State), the invoice acts as proof that allows the business to deduct VAT in the EU Member State concerned. No EU Member State may prevent this by requiring extra information in the invoice.

Businesses may always include information on their invoices additional to that described above.

## Legal texts
- [VAT Directive](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32006L0112)

| Date of transaction or payment (if different from invoice date) | - |
| VAT rate applied & amount payable | VAT amount payable (or the information needed to calculate it) |
| Breakdown of VAT amount payable by VAT rate or exemption | - |
| - | Specific, unambiguous reference to the initial invoice and the details that are being amended (on a credit note, debit note or other document treated as an invoice) |
| **Extra information required in some cases** |  |
| For exempt transactions: a reference to the appropriate (EU or national) legislation exempting it, or any other reference indicating it is exempt (at the choice of the supplier) |  |
| If the customer is liable for tax (i.e. under the reverse-charge procedure): the words ‘reverse charge’ |  |
| For intra-EU supply of a new means of transport: the details specified in Article 2(2)(b) of the [VAT Directive](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32006L0112) |  |
| If a margin scheme applies: a reference to the scheme involved (e.g. ‘margin scheme — travel agents’) |  |
| Self-billing (customer issues invoice instead of supplier): the words ‘self-billing’ |  |
| Supplier is operating a cash accounting system: the words ‘cash accounting’) |  |

Once all the information above is included on an invoice (depending on the case and EU Member State), the invoice acts as proof that allows the business to deduct VAT in the EU Member State concerned. No EU Member State may prevent this by requiring extra information in the invoice.

Businesses may always include information on their invoices additional to that described above.

## Legal texts
- [VAT Directive](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32006L0112)

- [VAT for businesses](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/value-added-tax-vat/vat-businesses_en)

content.thinking: I found that charge names, billing bases, and number/date formats vary across invoices (e.g., European decimal commas and DD.MM.YYYY dates), and my engine's `D()` and `day()` functions mishandle these cases. I'll fix both in the engine now, since it's free and doesn't affect the cache, before touching the extraction prompt.

.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
e = Path("harness/engine.py"); s = e.read_text()
a = s[s.index("def D(x)"):s.index("def money(x)")]
b = '''def D(x) -> Decimal | None:
    """A printed number -> Decimal, whichever way it is written: 1,234.56 / 1.234,56 / 1 234,56 / (12.50) / -12.50.
    The last separator is the decimal point when both appear; a lone comma is a decimal point unless it groups
    exactly three digits."""
    if x is None or isinstance(x, bool):
        return None
    s = re.sub(r"[\\s%$\\u20ac\\u00a3\\u20b9]|USD|INR|EUR|GBP|kg", "", str(x), flags=re.I)
    neg = s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")") or s.startswith("-")
    s = s.strip("()-+")
    if "," in s and "." in s:
        dec = "," if s.rfind(",") > s.rfind(".") else "."
        s = s.replace("." if dec == "," else ",", "").replace(dec, ".")
    elif "," in s:
        s = s.replace(",", "") if re.fullmatch(r"\\d{1,3}(,\\d{3})+", s) else s.replace(",", ".")
    elif s.count(".") > 1:
        s = s.replace(".", "")
    try:
        return -Decimal(s) if neg and s else (Decimal(s) if s else None)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None


def day(x) -> date | None:
    """ISO, DD.MM.YYYY, '4 Feb 2036', or a slash date whose order is unambiguous (a part above 12); else None."""
    from datetime import datetime
    t = str(x or "").strip()
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(t[:10])
    except ValueError:
        pass
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\\d{1,2})([./])(\\d{1,2})\\2(\\d{4})", t)
    if m:
        a, sep, b, y = int(m[1]), m[2], int(m[3]), int(m[4])
        d, mo = (a, b) if sep == "." or a > 12 else ((b, a) if b > 12 else (None, None))
        try:
            return date(y, mo, d) if d else None
        except ValueError:
            return None
    for fmt in ("%d %b %Y", "%d %B %Y", "%b %d, %Y", "%B %d, %Y"):
        try:
            return datetime.strptime(t, fmt).date()
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return None


'''
s = s.replace(a, b)
e.write_text(s)

                  ("12,5", "12.5"), ("1.234.567", "1234567"), ("USD 45.00", "45.00"), ("(12.50)", "-12.50"),
                  ("-12.50", "-12.50"), ("18.38%", "18.38"), ("\\u20ac 99,90", "99.90"), ("106 kg", "106"), ("", None),

content.text:
I searched, spending 6 Firecrawl credits, and used what I found for a free robustness fix. I did not change the extraction prompts or schemas. The reason is the one you flagged: a prompt change forces re-reads of every cached invoice, and that costs real money.

**What the research showed about real invoices**
- Charge labels vary a lot: SSC, X-ray fee, screening, BAF, FSC, THC.
- Billing bases vary: per kg, per piece or per AWB, with minimums.
- European invoices use decimal commas and DD.MM.YYYY dates.
- Credit and debit notes reference the original invoice.

**What I fixed**
- **Numbers:** `D()` stripped every comma, so "1.234,56" would have become 1.23456. It now reads 1,234.56, 1.234,56, 1 234,56, (12.50) and -12.50 correctly.
- **Dates:** `day()` returned nothing for "04.02.2036". It now reads DD.MM.YYYY, "4 Feb 2036", and slash dates when the order is clear. An ambiguous "03/06/2030" is still left to the extractor, which resolves it from the invoice's own dates.
- **Check:** `harness/test_parse.py` covers 24 cases. The parsing change needed no re-extraction. Practice is still 99.8, all 33 evals pass, and the engine test passes.

**What I didn't do, and why**
- **No label-synonym fallback.** Mapping unlisted labels like "SSC" to a code would risk false findings. Contracts list their own labels in Annex E, so an unlisted label stays unpriced.
- **No "minimum charge on an accessorial" support.** The glossary prices lines as rate × quantity, so adding it would be guesswork.
- **"Training" isn't a thing here.** Nothing is fine-tuned. The only places this research could go are the extraction prompts and my eval cases.

**Optional paid step, 2 agents (about 50 cents):** I'd add one eval mailbox with a European-format invoice, using decimal commas, dotted dates, VAT with reverse charge, and SSC/X-ray labels. It tests the extractor on a layout it hasn't seen, which is the part the free fix can't cover. I'll run it only if you say go.

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | Build what's asked, but name the lazier alternative in one line. User picks. |
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |
| **ultra** | YAGNI extremist. Deletion before addition. Ship the one-liner and challenge the rest of the requirement in the same breath. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- lite: "Done, cache added. FYI: `functools.lru_cache` covers this in one line if you'd rather not own a cache class."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."
- ultra: "No cache until a profiler says so. When it does: `@lru_cache`. A hand-rolled TTL cache class is a bug farm with a hit rate."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

def overcharges(w: World, out: list[dict]):
    for inv_id, (copy, _) in invoice_copies(w).items():
        f, ref = copy["f"], copy["ref"]
        c = w.contract_for(f.get("contract_id"))
        if c is None:
            continue
        pr = Pricer(w, c)
        inv_date = day(f.get("invoice_date"))
        diffs, ev, flags = [], [], {"pickup": set(), "lanes": set(), "levels": True, "issues": 0, "learned": None,
                                    "retro": False}
        conflict = None
        missing = None
        for awb, lines in shipments(f.get("lines") or []).items():
            if not awb:
                continue
            first = lines[0]
            pickup, psrc, pev = w.pickup(awb, first, ref, c)
            if pickup is None:
                continue
            lane = norm_lane(first.get("lane"))
            coded = [(ln, c.code_of(ln.get("description"))) for ln in lines]
            frt = [ln for ln, code in coded if code == FREIGHT]
            correct_frt = {}
            for ln in frt:
                cw = D(ln.get("quantity"))
                if cw is None:
                    continue
                res = pr.freight_sources(lane, pickup)
                if res["kind"] == "missing":
                    missing = {**res["missing"], "_inv": cites(cite(ref, ln))}
                    continue
                if res["kind"] == "unknown":
                    continue
                if res["kind"] == "conflict":
                    amts = []
                    for s in (res["a"], res["b"]):
                        a, e = pr.freight({**s, "msa_rows": (res["msa"] or {}).get("rows")}, cw)
                        amts.append((a, e, s))
                    if any(a is None for a, _, _ in amts):
                        continue
                    if amts[0][0] != amts[1][0]:
                        conflict = {"amts": amts, "line": ln, "clause": res.get("clause"), "pickup": pickup,
                                    "pev": pev, "lane": lane}
                        correct_frt[id(ln)] = None
                        flags["lanes"].add((c.id, lane, c.period_of(pickup)))
                        continue
                    res = {"kind": "ok", "src": res["a"], "msa": res["msa"]}   # they agree: nothing to decide
                src = res["src"]
                amt, e = pr.freight({**src, "msa_rows": (res["msa"] or {}).get("rows")}, cw)
                if amt is None:
                    continue
                correct_frt[id(ln)] = amt
                billed = D(ln.get("amount"))
                if res.get("fb"):
                    flags["learned"] = res["fb"]
                if src["level"] > 2:
                    flags["levels"] = False
                flags["lanes"].add((c.id, lane, c.period_of(pickup)))
                if billed is not None and billed != amt:
                    diffs.append(billed - amt)
                    ev += [cite(ref, ln)] + e + pev + [cite(c.ref, c.clause("pricing_date"), "text_src")]
                    flags["pickup"].add(psrc)
                    if src["kind"] in ("amendment", "annex") and src["received"] > copy["received"] \
                            and (src["eff"] or date.max) <= pickup:
                        flags["retro"] = True
            base_frt = None
            if frt and all(id(ln) in correct_frt for ln in frt):
                vals = [correct_frt[id(ln)] for ln in frt]
                base_frt = None if any(v is None for v in vals) else sum(vals, ZERO)
            for ln, code in coded:
                billed = D(ln.get("amount"))
                if billed is None or code in (None, FREIGHT) or code in NOT_PRICED:
                    continue
                correct, e = line_correct(w, pr, c, code, ln, awb, pickup, base_frt, lines)
                if correct is None:
                    continue
                if billed > correct:
                    diffs.append(billed - correct)
                    ev += [cite(ref, ln)] + e
                    if code == FUEL:
                        flags["pickup"].add(psrc)
                        ev += pev
        if missing:
            out.append(item("overcharge", {"invoice_id": inv_id}, "cannot_determine",
                            evidence=[missing.pop("_inv")] + [missing.pop("_cite")],
                            missing={k: v for k, v in missing.items() if not k.startswith("_") and k != "eff"},
                            contract=c, outbound=True, safe=True, lanes=flags["lanes"]))
            continue
        pos = sum((d for d in diffs if d > 0), ZERO)
        if conflict:
            ln = conflict["line"]
            billed_f = D(ln.get("amount"))
            fuel_lines = [x for x in shipments(f.get("lines") or [])[(ln.get("awb") or "").strip().upper()]
                          if c.code_of(x.get("description")) == FUEL]
            pct, fev = pr.fuel_pct(conflict["pickup"])
            billed_total = billed_f + sum((D(x.get("amount")) or ZERO for x in fuel_lines), ZERO)
            totals = []
            for a, e, s in conflict["amts"]:
                fuel = rhu(pct / 100 * a) if (pct is not None and fuel_lines) else ZERO
                totals.append(a + fuel)
            lo, hi = max(ZERO, billed_total - max(totals)), billed_total - min(totals)
            if hi + pos > 0:
                (a1, e1, s1), (a2, e2, s2) = conflict["amts"]
                ev2 = [cite(ref, ln)] + e1 + e2 + [conflict["clause"]] + conflict["pev"]
                out.append(item("overcharge", {"invoice_id": inv_id}, "conflict", rng=(lo + pos, hi + pos),
                                evidence=ev2, contract=c, outbound=False, lanes=flags["lanes"],
                                learned=flags["learned"]))
            continue
        if pos <= 0:
            continue
        amount, fxev = to_usd(pr, f, pos)
        if amount is None:
            out.append(missing_fx(pr, inv_id, "overcharge", ref, f))
            continue
        out.append(item("overcharge", {"invoice_id": inv_id}, "finding", amount=amount, evidence=ev + fxev,
                        contract=c, outbound=True, pickup=flags["pickup"], lanes=flags["lanes"],
                        safe=flags["levels"] and flags["pickup"] <= {"tracking", "email"},
                        learned=flags["learned"], retro=flags["retro"], currency=f.get("currency"), native=pos))

def build_state(state: Path) -> None:

    for f in sorted(BOX.rglob("*.eml")):
        group = DOCS.read_email(f, f.parent.name)
        rec = {"meta": group[0].meta, "docs": []}
        for d in group:

def main() -> int:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        build_state(Path(tmp))
        for mode, act in (("supervised", "draft:dispute"), ("autonomous", "execute:dispute")):
            rep = engine.build(Path(tmp), date(2032, 8, 31), mode, [], {})
            got = {i["invoice_id"]: i for i in rep["findings"]}

Ponytail is on. I added the promised free fixes to `engine.py`:

- **Margin step-down cashback:** the extra margin billed after a quarter's spend crosses the step-down threshold now becomes one cashback item per quarter, never per-invoice overcharges. It reuses the existing cashback loop and credit-note subtraction, and splits per-invoice spend out of `qualifying()` so both share it. Two choices are guesses, marked `ponytail:` in the code: the threshold counts Qualifying Spend, and the credit is claimable at quarter end.
- **Quoted-waiver holder:** the missing original's holder is now the author's own Schedule 1 entry, or the Key Account Manager if they aren't listed for waivers. The missing document's name now contains "waiver".
- **Conflict blocking:** an open rate conflict now blocks unattended action only for findings that rely on that rate (freight and its fuel), per the glossary's "(and charge and period)". Before, it also blocked accessorial overcharges on the same lane.
- **Duplicates:** a pass-through, duty or margin line billed twice is now caught. Only late-fee and tax lines are excluded.

All checks came from the cache, with no extraction or API calls. Nothing regressed: practice is still 99.8 in both modes, all 33 evals pass, and the exam sheet is unchanged at $8,165.33. The margin rule has only been checked against hand-written facts (`test_engine.py`), because none of the contracts I have include the clause.

Skipped: the supervised-execute assertion. `action()` can only return `execute:*` in autonomous mode, so the check would never run.

The review workflow (`engine-glossary-review`) is running in the background with at most 12 agents. When it finishes I'll fix the confirmed findings and rerun the cached checks. None of this is committed yet; say if you want it committed.

files, or persist anything.

This is an unsafe autonomous execute: it counts double, and 3 or more trigger the hard gate. Confidence also misses its 0.12 pickup penalty.
FIX: engine.py:732-738: run `flags["pickup"].add(psrc)` for every line where billed > correct, not only under `if code == FUEL:`. Leave the lanes and pev additions as they are.

### actions-ids-asof/F4 [low] build (engine.py:1459-1469), plus apply_decisions override
SCENARIO: Feedback rejects an overcharge (or overrides its amount) on invoice INV-9. A later register shows INV-9 open, with a due date 1 to 14 days after as_of.
EXPECTED: For reject, the principal is the full open amount, because nothing is disputed any more. For override, the principal is the open amount less the overridden amount.
ACTUAL: `disputed` is computed from the items before apply_decisions runs (line 1469). The rejected finding's amount, or the pre-override amount, is still subtracted, so late_fee_risk.amount_usd is wrong. Moving the call alone would not fix override: disputed reads it['_native'] first, and override never updates _native.
FIX: In build, add `items = apply_decisions(w, items)` right after the `for fn in (overcharges, duplicates, waived, late_fees)` loop, before disputed is computed. Keep the later call, which handles the portfolio items. In apply_decisions' override branch, add `if str(it.get("_currency") or "USD").upper() == "USD": it["_native"] = amt`. ### actions-ids-asof/F5 [low] add_credit (engine.py:1330) -> action()
SCENARIO: The rebate clause says the credit is due 30 days after quarter end. For 2035-Q1 that is 2035-03-31 + 30 = 2035-04-30, and a batch reports --as-of 2035-04-30, a month-end date like the practice batch dates.
EXPECTED: as_of is not before the due date, so the credit is due: draft:claim_credit (execute:claim_credit in autonomous when safe).
ACTUAL: outbound = w.as_of > due is False on the due date itself, so the action is internal:track_credit and the key also leaves the threshold sum.

SCENARIO: Invoice A has a conflict on lane L1 (unranked amendment against a rate notice) and, on another AWB, a plain freight or fuel overcharge on lane L2. Invoice B has a clean, under-$5,000 overcharge on L2 only, with tracking pickup dates. Report run with --mode autonomous.

At line 762, pass `lanes=flags["clanes"]`. The proposed one-liner `lanes={(c.id, conflict["lane"], c.period_of(conflict["pickup"]))}` also works when an invoice has only one conflicting AWB.

## [regressions/medium] Pricer.freight_sources, engine.py:582-583 (and Pricer.fx, engine.py:488-489)
PROBLEM: The diff added off_key(fb, invs) to World.authorised with the default invs=(). These two callers don't pass invs. off_key(fb, ()) is always True for a one_off fact, so a one-off sender_authority confirmation for 'rates' or 'treasury' is now ignored on every invoice, its own key included. Before the diff it applied (to every invoice). I confirmed off_key(fb, ()) == True with a snippet.
TRIGGER: Bo Example is not on Schedule 1 for rates. His rate notice for lane L is in force on the pickup date. Invoice TX-1 bills lane L at Bo's notice rate, which is below the MSA rate. Before the fix, without his authority, TX-1 is measured against the MSA, so the result is either no overcharge or one measured against the MSA. Feedback item: decision confirm, fact sender_authority, subject.person 'Bo Exa
FIX: Pass the Pricer's invoice. At line 582-583: `w.authorised(c, "rates", email, ..., n["received"], c.carrier, {self.inv})`. At line 488: `self.w.authorised(self.c, "treasury", ..., r["received"], None, {self.inv})`. Also build the Pricer with inv_id where invoice keys convert currency (duplicates, waived, late_fees: Pricer(w, c, inv_id)).

## [regressions/medium] disputed_by_invoice, engine.py:1535-1541, consumed by late_fees, engine.py:1153
PROBLEM: The new disputed map counts a same-number resend duplicate at the full invoice total (native=total) against that invoice number. late_fees now subtracts disputed from the target's principal. When the resent invoice is also the target of a late fee, its base drops to 0 and the whole fee is called not owed. What we dispute there is the second payment request, not the principal of the original, which was owed and paid late.
TRIGGER: TX-1: USD 4200.07, due 2032-12-12, paid 2033-01-01 (20 days late, grace 5, 1.86%/month). TX-1 is resent on 2033-01-10 asking for payment, and the ledger shows it paid, so duplicate:TX-1 is a finding of 4200.07. Invoice INV-F bills 'Late fee on TX-1: USD 4200.07 overdue, month 1 @ 1.86%' 78.12.
FIX: Tag the resend item in duplicates() (line 977: add resend=True to item(...)). In disputed_by_invoice add `and not it.get("_resend")` to the condition.

## [regressions/low] overcharges conflict branch, engine.py:774-784
PROBLEM: The new multi-shipment range adds up every conflicted AWB's 'a' side (amendment) and 'b' side (notice), then takes max/min of those two totals. Conflicts on different lanes, or in different rate periods, are separate decisions: resolve_conflict and precedence work per contract and lane. So the higher and lower correct amounts are each lane's max and min, added up. When the amendment is lower on one lane and the notice is lower on another, adding by side cancels the two out and shrinks the range.
TRIGGER: One invoice has two AWBs with no fuel lines, both picked up while an unranked (cl. 13.3) amendment and a Schedule 1 rate notice are in force. AWB A1, lane L1, 113 kg: amendment 2.88 (325.44), notice 3.03 (342.39), billed 342.39. AWB A2, lane L2, 100 kg: amendment 3.10 (310.00), notice 2.95 (295.00), billed 310.00.
FIX: Keep the per-AWB totals with fuel, but group them by cf['lane'] before taking extremes: `g = by_lane.setdefault(cf['lane'], [ZERO, ZERO]); g[0] += a_tot; g[1] += b_tot`. Then use hi_corr = sum(max(g)) and lo_corr = sum(min(g)) over the groups, with lo = max(0, billed - hi_corr) + pos and hi = billed - lo_corr + pos.

## [regressions/low] margin_step_down, engine.py:1375-1380
PROBLEM: The new `unknown` flag is set whenever any invoice in the quarter has no FX rate, even when that can't change the answer. The step-down only affects invoices after the crossing. If the FX-less invoice is the last one in the quarter, or no later invoice carries a MARGIN line, nothing can be overbilled. The diff still emits a cannot_determine cashback key where the old code emitted nothing. GLOSSARY: 'It isn't cannot_determine when the missing document couldn't change the answer.'
TRIGGER: INR contract with handling margin 10%, stepping to 8% after USD 50,000 Qualifying Spend in a quarter. 2036-Q1 has two invoices: one dated 2036-01-15 with an Annex F row (QS about USD 20,000), and the quarter's last invoice, dated 2036-03-20, in a month after the last Annex F row. The quarter is closed at as_of.
FIX: Track the gap without flagging it: `blind = blind or spend is None` in place of setting unknown. Inside `if crossed or blind:`, set unknown only when this later invoice has a MARGIN line while it is still unknown whether the quarter crossed (blind and not crossed). Keep the `usd is None` case as it is.

## [regressions/low] quarters, engine.py:1287-1295, and the contract-year loop in cashback, engine.py:1267
PROBLEM: The diff removed the contract-end bound from both loops instead of replacing it with an end that counts extensions, which is what CB-1 asked for. Quarters and contract years after the term are now evaluated for any invoice still dated under the contract id. The improvement credit is a flat percent with no threshold, so one late-dated invoice creates a promised credit for a contract year the contract never had.
TRIGGER: MSA effective 2030-04-02, end 2031-04-01, no extension, improvement credit 1.76% of the Contract Year's QS. A shipment picked up 2031-03-30 is invoiced 2031-04-03 under the same contract id, with QS USD 3,000.00. Report run with --as-of 2032-04-15.
FIX: Bound both loops by the term end, counting extensions: `end = max([c.end] + [day(i.get('new_end_date')) for i in w.instruments_for(c) if i.get('signed_by_both') and day(i.get('new_end_date'))], default=None)` (drop None values). In quarters, keep a quarter only if `not end or quarter_bounds(q)[0] <= end`. In the CY loop, stop when `end and add_years(c.effective, n - 1) > end`.

## [hard-gates/medium] engine.py overcharges(), conflict branch lines 774-791 (uhi/ulo built from billed - min/max(ta,tb) + pos)
PROBLEM: When the conflicted freight is billed below both sources' correct amounts, the price ambiguity can't change the answer, but the code still goes down the conflict path. The negative 'billed - min(ta,tb)' then offsets the plain overcharge on other lines. Result: a false conflict with an inverted range, or the real overcharge is dropped entirely.
TRIGGER: Unranked precedence. Invoice I-1 has AWB A1 on lane L1 (amendment 70/kg, Schedule 1 rate notice 75/kg, 100 kg, billed 6990.00) and AWB A2 on lane L2 (MSA 80/kg, 100 kg, billed 8050.00). Both pickups come from tracking. I ran this with engine.build.
FIX: In the `if conflicts:` block, compute billed/ta/tb as now, then wrap the emit-and-`continue` in `if billed > min(ta, tb):`. Otherwise fall through to the normal `pos` finding path. The conflict lanes are then not open.

## [hard-gates/medium] engine.py Pricer.freight_sources lines 595-603 (resolve_conflict check `if fb and not (amd['eff'] > valid_from)`)
PROBLEM: When a signed amendment that takes effect after the resolve_conflict feedback's valid_from is in force, the code skips the feedback and drops back to the 'unranked' rule. It reports a fresh conflict, but GLOSSARY says 'A later signed amendment still beats it'.
TRIGGER: Feedback resolve_conflict + precedence for contract C-1, lane L1, valid_from 2040-04-01, use 'rate notice' (or 'amendment'). Then AMD-2, signed by both, effective 2040-05-01, sets L1 to 72/kg while the Schedule 1 notice (75/kg) is still in force. Invoice I-2: pickup 2040-05-10 from tracking, 100 kg, billed 8000.00. I ran this with engine.build.
FIX: Change the branch to `if fb:` and set `later = amd['eff'] and vf and amd['eff'] > vf`. Return `{'kind':'ok','src': amd if later or 'notice' not in use else notice, 'msa': msa, 'fb': None if later else fb}`.

## [hard-gates/low] engine.py late_fees() line 1151 (`w.due_date(tgt, c, ..., {b[1] for b in bills})` computed once per target)
PROBLEM: The extended due date is worked out once for the target invoice, using the set of every invoice that bills its fees. A one_off sender_authority item keyed to one fee-bearing invoice therefore also moves the due date for the other fee invoice's key. That spreads a one-off decision beyond its key.
TRIGGER: T-1 is due 2040-01-10 and paid 2040-02-25; the contract has 2%/month and 5 grace days. Pat (not on Schedule 1) emails an extension of T-1 to 2040-02-20. F-2 bills the month-1 fee (20.00) and F-3 bills the month-2 fee (20.00). Feedback: confirm sender_authority for Pat, payment_terms, scope one_off applies_to invoice_id F-2. I ran this with engine.build.
FIX: Move `due, xev, fb = w.due_date(tgt, c, day(row.get('due_date')), {inv_id})` and `owed = fee_owed(...)` inside the `for _, inv_id, copy, c, lns in bills:` loop, so each fee invoice is judged with its own key. Keep the cum/extra arithmetic unchanged.

## [hard-gates/low] engine.py margin_step_down() line 1376 (`unknown = unknown or spend is None`)
PROBLEM: Any invoice in the quarter whose INR spend has no Annex F rate makes the whole margin_step_down key cannot_determine. That happens even when the missing rate can't change the answer: the invoice comes before any crossing and no later invoice carries a MARGIN line to step down.
TRIGGER: INR contract with handling_margin 12% -> 8% after 100,000.00. Annex F has 2040-01 and 2040-02 but not 2040-03. Three invoices (Jan, Feb, Mar), each with 1,000 INR cost and a 120 INR margin line; the March invoice is the last of Q1. as_of 2040-04-30. I ran this with engine.build.
FIX: Set unknown only when the missing spend could matter. Keep `gap = gap or spend is None` after each invoice. - **Resent invoices and late fees:** a resent-invoice duplicate counted its full total as disputed. That pushed the late-fee base to zero, so a fee that was really owed got reported as not owed.
- **One-off authority:** one-off rates and treasury authority stopped applying anywhere, even on the invoice it was granted for.

The other 16 fixes:
- **Conflicts:** the range is now taken per lane, so two lanes can no longer cancel each other out. No conflict is raised when the invoice is billed below both answers; the real overcharge on another lane is reported instead.
- **Late fees:** each fee invoice is judged against its own key's due date, so a one-off approval no longer spreads to the next fee invoice. Lines that name their month are checked month by month. Disputed amounts come off the printed principal.
- **Feedback:** a later signed amendment now overrides a precedence decision, as the glossary says.
- **Automation-directed text:** pickup events and exchange rates written to "the AI" are no longer used as facts.
- **Unattended actions:** a document request only goes out unattended when Schedule 1 names a person to send it to.
- **Smaller fixes:** cashback periods follow the term end, extensions included. The margin step-down only needs a missing exchange rate when that rate could change the answer. Annual rebates use the right due date. An overridden conflict now counts as disputed. A charge repeated within one invoice is still caught.

All of this was checked from the cache, with no API spend:
- **Practice card:** 99.8 in both modes, all hard gates clear, escalation at 4%.
- **Evals:** 35 of 35 pass. Two new one-off authority cases are included, and they fail on the old engine.
- **Exam sheet:** unchanged at $8,165.33.
- **Reproductions:** I replayed three of the verifiers' triggers (resent invoice, conflict billed below both answers, per-lane range) and all now give the glossary's answer.
- **`make validate`:** passes 9 of 9.

SOLUTION.md and DESIGN.md now say plainly that margin step-down, other promised credits, and band-by-band and annual rebates are only checked on hand-written facts, because no contract in the data has those clauses.

The engine changes and the doc updates are all uncommitted. Should I commit them to `harness-baseline`? The ponytail audit cuts are still unapplied, and the live API check is still pending a working key.

from pathlib import Path
d = Path("harness/docs.py"); s = d.read_text()
a = '''# ---- XLSX (same as grader/extract.py)'''
b = '''def ocr_pages(pngs: list[bytes]) -> list[str]:
    """Local OCR (rapidocr) for a scan, used when the vision model can't be reached: text boxes regrouped into lines
    by their vertical centre, left to right. It drops spaces inside a box ("274kg"); the extractor copes."""
    import numpy as np
    from PIL import Image
    from rapidocr_onnxruntime import RapidOCR
    ocr, pages = RapidOCR(), []
    for png in pngs:
        res, _ = ocr(np.array(Image.open(io.BytesIO(png)).convert("RGB")))
        rows: list[list] = []
        for box, text, _conf in sorted(res or [], key=lambda r: (r[0][0][1] + r[0][2][1]) / 2):
            y = (box[0][1] + box[2][1]) / 2
            if rows and abs(rows[-1][0] - y) < 12:      # ponytail: fixed 12 px line tolerance at 200 dpi
                rows[-1][1].append((box[0][0], text))
            else:
                rows.append([y, [(box[0][0], text)]])
        pages.append("\\n".join(" ".join(t for _, t in sorted(ws)) for _, ws in rows))
    return pages


# ---- XLSX (same as grader/extract.py)'''
assert s.count(a) == 1; d.write_text(s.replace(a, b))
h = Path("harness/harness.py"); t = h.read_text()
a = '''        for d, pages in zip(scans, ex.map(lambda d: guarded(llm.transcribe, state, d.sha, d.scan_pngs), scans)):
            if pages:
                d.pages = pages'''
b = '''        for d, pages in zip(scans, ex.map(lambda d: guarded(llm.transcribe, state, d.sha, d.scan_pngs), scans)):
            d.pages = pages or guarded(lambda _, p: DOCS.ocr_pages(p), d.ref, d.scan_pngs) or d.pages'''
assert t.count(a) == 1; h.write_text(t.replace(a, b))
EOF

content.thinking: Based on FedEx's invoice formats (summary-then-detail layouts, columnar duty/VAT invoices, European date/currency conventions), I'll build three new Velloran eval mailboxes to test edge cases the current data lacks: summary rows that shouldn't double-count charges, a wide spreadsheet with mismatched fuel percentages, and a European-format invoice with reverse-charge VAT and a DG fee on dry ice.

from pathlib import Path
b = Path("evals/build_cases.py"); s = b.read_text()
a = '''BUILDERS = ['''
new = '''def eu(x) -> str:                     # 1.234,56
    return f"{rhu(x):,.2f}".replace(",", "X").replace(".", ",").replace("X", ".")


def case_summary_detail():
    """A courier-style bill: a summary page (one total per waybill), then a detail block per shipment on page 2.
    Dates DD/MM/YYYY; fuel stated as a footnote percentage. The summary rows are not extra charges."""
    issued, c1, c2 = date(2036, 2, 18), date(2036, 2, 10), date(2036, 2, 12)
    k1, k2 = D("214.0"), D("120.0")
    f1 = rhu(k1 * D("5.30"))                               # period B rate on a period A collection
    u1, s1, d1 = rhu(f1 * D(fuel_pct(c1)) / 100), rhu(k1 * D("0.14")), D("98.40")
    f2 = rhu(k2 * rate("USW5-USC2", k2, c2))
    u2 = rhu(f2 * D(fuel_pct(c2)) / 100)
    t1, t2 = f1 + u1 + s1 + d1, f2 + u2
    cf = rhu(k1 * rate("USN4-INE3", k1, c1))
    over = (f1 - cf) + (u1 - rhu(cf * D(fuel_pct(c1)) / 100))
    hd = "Velloran Air Cargo Inc. | Billing document VLA-36-02001 | Agreement VLA-US-AIR-07"
    p1 = [hd, "BILLING DOCUMENT VLA-36-02001", f"Issued {issued:%d/%m/%Y}   Payment due {issued + timedelta(30):%d/%m/%Y}",
          "Customer Brackwater Biologics Inc.", "SUMMARY OF SHIPMENTS",
          "Waybill Collected Service Pieces Weight Taxable Non taxable Total (USD)",
          f"VA90010001 {c1:%d/%m/%Y} Priority air 4 214.0 kg 0.00 {m(t1)} {m(t1)}",
          f"VA90010002 {c2:%d/%m/%Y} Priority air 2 120.0 kg 0.00 {m(t2)} {m(t2)}",
          f"Amount payable USD {m(t1 + t2)}", "Details of every charge follow on page 2."]
    p2 = [hd, "SHIPMENT DETAIL",
          f"Waybill VA90010001  Collected {c1:%d/%m/%Y}  Route USN4-INE3  Billed weight: 214.0 kg",
          "Charges Amount", f"Linehaul 214.0 kg x 5.30 {m(f1)}", f"FSC {m(u1)}", f"X-ray screening 214.0 kg x 0.14 {m(s1)}",
          f"Door drop 1 consignment {m(d1)}", f"Shipment total USD {m(t1)}",
          f"Waybill VA90010002  Collected {c2:%d/%m/%Y}  Route USW5-USC2  Billed weight: 120.0 kg",
          "Charges Amount", f"Linehaul 120.0 kg x {rate('USW5-USC2', k2, c2)} {m(f2)}", f"FSC {m(u2)}",
          f"Shipment total USD {m(t2)}",
          f"A fuel surcharge (FSC) of {fuel_pct(c1)} % of linehaul applies to collections in February 2036."]
    box = {"batch_01": [msa_email(1),
                        mail_att(2, BILLING, issued + timedelta(1), "Billing document VLA-36-02001",
                                 "Dear Quentin,\\n\\nYour billing document VLA-36-02001 is attached (summary and detail)."
                                 "\\n\\nVelloran Billing", "VLA-36-02001.pdf", pdf([p1, p2])),
                        tracking(3, date(2036, 2, 29), [("VA90010001", "Collected from shipper", c1, "USN4"),
                                                        ("VA90010002", "Collected from shipper", c2, "USW5")])]}
    return "summary_detail", box, [
        ("ev_summary_detail_overcharge", "summary page then detail blocks; period B rate on a period A waybill",
         "2036-03-31", "supervised", {"invoice_id": "VLA-36-02001", "class": "overcharge"},
         {"verdict": "finding", "amount_usd": p(over), "action": "draft:dispute"},
         "priced from the detail block on page 2; dates are day-first (issued 18/02)"),
        ("ev_summary_not_duplicate", "the summary rows repeat each shipment's total: not a duplicate charge",
         "2036-03-31", "supervised", {"invoice_id": "VLA-36-02001", "class": "duplicate"}, {"verdict": "no_finding"},
         "a summary line is not a second billing of the shipment"),
    ]


def case_wide_statement():
    """A spreadsheet with one row per waybill and the charges in columns. Row 2 bills fuel at the wrong month's %."""
    issued, c1, c2 = date(2036, 3, 20), date(2036, 3, 4), date(2036, 3, 9)

def case_eu_format():

          "Pos. Luftfrachtbrief / Waybill Leistung / Service Abholung / Collected Menge / Qty Preis / Rate Betrag / Amount",
          *[f"{i} VA90030003 {lab} {c:%d.%m.%Y} {q} {r} {eu(a)}" for i, (lab, q, r, a) in enumerate(lines, 1)],

    msg = eml(BILLING, AP_ADDR, at(issued + timedelta(1), 9), "Rechnung VLA-36-03003",

    box = {"batch_01": [msa_email(1), ("0002.eml", msg),
                        tracking(3, date(2036, 4, 30), [("VA90030003", "Collected from shipper", c, "USE4")])]}
    return "eu_format", box, [

         "2036-05-15", "supervised", {"invoice_id": "VLA-36-03003", "class": "overcharge"},
         {"verdict": "finding", "amount_usd": "260.00", "action": "draft:dispute"},

def mail_att(n: int, frm: str, when: date, subject: str, body: str, name: str, data: bytes) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
    return f"{n:04d}.eml", eml(frm, AP_ADDR, at(when, 9), subject, body, [(name, data)])

b.write_text(s)

I ran the 13 extractions you approved, and the harness handled all three new invoice layouts correctly on the first run. It was the only paid step.

- **Summary-then-detail PDF:** overcharge of 31.18, priced from the detail block on page 2 and quoted there. The summary rows were not mistaken for duplicate charges, and the dates were read day-first.
- **Wide spreadsheet** (charges in columns): overcharge of 10.84, from fuel billed at December's percentage instead of March's.
- **European invoice** (decimal commas, DD.MM.YYYY, reverse-charge VAT line): overcharge of 260.00 for the DG fee on a dry-ice-only shipment.

Every quote is on the page it cites. Everything else held:
- Evals: 39 of 39 pass, 37 of them mine.
- Practice card: still 99.8 in both modes.
- Exam sheet: unchanged at $8,165.33.

Since none of the three cases failed, they didn't uncover a bug. They do now guard these layouts against regressions. To your second question: OCR is now in the harness as a fallback. The vision model still reads scans first, and local `rapidocr` takes over if that call fails. It isn't exercised in the eval suite, since every scan in the cache already has a vision transcript; I checked it separately on the exam scan.

Everything since the first commit is still uncommitted: the 45 engine fixes, margin step-down, the OCR fallback, the new evals and the doc updates. Should I commit it to `harness-baseline`?

content.thinking: I've confirmed the rate-class codes (M for minimum, N/Q for weight-break rates), and I'll now build four new test variants: D tests IATA waybill formatting without a collection-date column, E tests a minimum charge billed at the wrong lane, F tests a bracketed credit note with a rebill, and G tests PDF footer text aimed at tricking automated readers on an invoice with a real overcharge.
